**IS212 (AY 2026/27 T1) – Customer Briefing**

**** Please Read This First ****

For the IS212 project, you will build the first release of a system using the scrum process.

In this document, you will find a briefing from the (mock) customer describing their desired system.

Please note that -

This customer briefing is (initially) **deliberately ambiguous. Why?** No real-world customer knows _precisely_ what they want on day 1, and there may be edge cases or conflicting expectations that have not yet been considered.

You can disambiguate the briefing by 'meeting' the customer (role played by your section's instructor) during the scheduled Q&A sessions over the next few weeks. Questions through other channels will not be answered.

**Each section has a different 'customer'.** Please only consider clarifications provided by your section's customer, as clarifications in other sections may not be consistent.

The customer briefing is quite wide-ranging. Don't panic! You will NOT build the entire system. The customer **will eventually clarify the core functionalities to cover in your first release** (i.e., your Week 12 submission). Wait for these to be identified in Week 4 before you start coding, and work on creating epics/user stories for your product backlog in the meantime.

The IS212 project instructions will be released on Friday, Week 3 (6pm). These instructions will list the artefacts expected in your submission and the grading rubrics, which emphasise the **scrum process, requirements discovery, software quality, and your documentation of these activities** more than the final product alone.

Until the project instructions are released, use Weeks 2-4 to understand the customer's needs and translate them into a product backlog of epics and user stories. We do not recommend sprinting until Week 4, especially as the customer has not yet identified the core functionalities to be implemented in the first release.

  

**Customer Briefing: Event Planning and Venue Booking System**

**1. Organisation**

ConnectSphere Event Services is a regional organisation that provides professional event planning and venue services to organisations across Southeast Asia. The company organises a wide variety of events, such as conferences, seminars, workshops, etc.

It operates and owns several event facilities within Singapore. ConnectSphere also maintains equipment and supporting resources commonly required for events. ConnectSphere currently has approximately 500 staff for its operations, taking on the role of **Event Coordinators**, **Venue Staff**, and **Technical Support Staff**.

As the organization expands, the number of events, venues, resources, clients, and participants that must be coordinated has increased significantly. ConnectSphere would therefore like to modernise the way it manages its events.

The proposed system will be used by internal and external users.

**2. Background**

ConnectSphere currently relies on a mixture of email, spreadsheets, shared calendars, messaging applications, online forms, and manually maintained documents to organise events. Information for a single event may therefore be spread across several places and managed by different employees.

A typical event begins when an external **Event Organiser** approaches ConnectSphere with an event to host or support. The Event Organiser is responsible for providing the initial requirements and communicating with ConnectSphere about the event, and provides preliminary information such as the purpose and type of event, preferred date and time, expected number of attendees, general programme, room-layout preferences, accessibility requirements, equipment requirements, registration requirements, and any other special arrangements.

An **Event Coordinator** is then assigned to the request and acts as the main liaison for the Event Organiser, who will review the request and contact the Event Organiser for any clarifications and coordination before confirmation.

For example, the Event Organiser may request a "large room" without specifying the expected attendance or may request a hybrid event without explaining what video-conferencing facilities are required.

Once the basic requirements are sufficiently clear, the Event Coordinator works with **Venue Staff** to identify a suitable venue. Venue Staff maintain information about ConnectSphere's rooms and spaces and are responsible for deciding whether the requested venue can be made available for the event.

Venue suitability may depend on several factors, such as the proposed date and time, maximum capacity, supported room layouts, accessibility, available facilities, existing bookings, operating hours, setup requirements, and the turnaround time required between consecutive events. A venue may also be unavailable because of maintenance, renovation, safety restrictions, or another internal activity.

Some events also require technical equipment and support. In these cases, **Technical Support Staff** review the requested equipment and technical support. They maintain records of available equipment, determine whether sufficient equipment can be reserved, and may also be assigned to support an event on-site.

Equipment may already be reserved for another event, located at another venue, damaged, or undergoing maintenance. The planning process may therefore involve several rounds of communication before an event can be confirmed.

Once the essential arrangements have been made, the Event Coordinator can confirm the event with the Event Organiser. For events that require registration, Attendees may subsequently register through the system and receive the event information.

Changes frequently occur after an event has been proposed or even after it has been confirmed. For example:

·       The Event Organiser may request a different date or time.

·       Expected attendance may increase or decrease.

·       Additional equipment or technical support may be requested.

·       The programme may be extended, shortened, or split into multiple sessions.

·       A booked venue may become unavailable because of an operational issue.

·       Reserved equipment may become unavailable because of damage or maintenance.

·       The Event Organiser may postpone or cancel the event due to unforeseen circumstances.

·       Registration numbers may reach the event capacity earlier than expected.

Such changes can affect arrangements that have already been made. Increasing attendance from 80 to 150 people may make the selected venue unsuitable. Changing an event date may create a venue or equipment conflict. Extending an event may affect the turnaround time needed before another booking. ConnectSphere therefore expects the proposed system to help users identify and manage these relationships.

The current process creates several difficulties:

·       Event requests may be incomplete, duplicated, or difficult to track.

·       Event Coordinators may maintain separate spreadsheets or personal notes, creating different versions of the same event information.

·       Event Organisers may be unsure whether an event, venue, or equipment arrangement has been approved or confirmed.

·       Venue Staff may receive incomplete or outdated event requirements.

·       The same venue or equipment may accidentally be considered available for more than one event.

·       Insufficient setup or turnaround time may be left between consecutive events.

·       Last-minute changes may not reach all affected staff or attendees.

·       Cancelled events may continue to occupy venue or equipment reservations.

·       Technical Support Staff may receive insufficient notice about upcoming equipment or support requirements.

·       Attendees may receive outdated dates, times, or venue information after an event changes.

·       It is difficult to identify which upcoming events still have incomplete arrangements.

·       It is difficult to determine who changed important event information and when the change occurred.

ConnectSphere would therefore like to develop a custom-built Event Planning and Venue Booking System that provides a single platform for its processes.

**3. Target group of users**

The system will be used by ConnectSphere and external users. The roles below are the roles referred to throughout this customer briefing.

|**Role**|**Internal / External**|**Main Responsibility**|
|---|---|---|
|Event Organiser|External|Client representative who has an event to organize and communicates event requirements to ConnectSphere.|
|Event Coordinator|Internal|They are assigned to coordinate the overall planning of an event and act as the main internal point of contact.|
|Venue Staff|Internal|They are responsible for venue information, availability, booking decisions, and physical venue preparation.|
|Technical Support Staff|Internal|They are responsible for equipment, technical requirements, equipment reservations, and technical support for events.|
|Attendee|External|Participant who registers for and attends an event.|

**4. Application features**

The following describes the broad functionality ConnectSphere is considering for the proposed system. The customer briefing is intentionally wide-ranging, and the first software release may not implement every functionality described below.

|**Functionality Area**|**Description**|
|---|---|
|User Authorisation and Authentication|Allow users to securely access the system. Access to information and functionality depends on whether the user is an Event Organiser, Event Coordinator, Venue Staff member, Technical Support Staff member, or Attendee.|
|User Profile Management|Users can maintain relevant profile information such as name, organisation, contact details, and communication preferences. Internal users may also have information relating to their department or responsibilities.|
|Client Management|ConnectSphere can maintain information about external client organisations. Multiple Event Organisers may belong to the same organisation, and an organisation may have several past and upcoming events.|
|Event Request Creation|Event Organisers can create event requests containing information such as the event name, description, purpose, preferred dates, expected attendance, venue requirements, accessibility needs, and other planning information.|
|Draft Event Requests|Event Organisers can save an event request before submission so that incomplete information can be completed or reviewed later.|
|Event Categories|Events can be classified into categories such as conference, workshop, training session, exhibition, meeting, seminar, networking event, or any other type defined by ConnectSphere.|
|Event Review and Approval|Event Coordinators can review submitted requests, request amendments or clarification, approve requests, or reject requests where appropriate.|
|Coordinator Assignment|Events can be assigned to an Event Coordinator responsible for managing the planning process. Reassignment may be required when staff responsibilities or availability change.|
|Event Status Management|Events progress through suitable statuses so that users can understand their current stage, for example draft, submitted, under review, approved, planning, awaiting arrangements, confirmed, completed, cancelled, or rejected.|
|Event Information Management|Authorised users can update relevant event information during planning. The system should distinguish between ordinary edits and changes that may affect arrangements already confirmed.|
|Event Programme and Agenda|Event Organisers or Event Coordinators can record the programme for an event, including sessions, breaks, presentations, or other scheduled activities.|
|Multi-Session Events|Some events may contain several sessions within the same day or across multiple days. Sessions may have different timings or operational requirements.|

|**Functionality Area**|**Description**|
|---|---|
|Recurring or Similar Events|Where useful, information from a previous or recurring event may be reused to reduce repeated data entry, while still allowing the new event to have different dates and requirements.|
|Comments and Discussion|Event Organisers and relevant internal users can exchange comments, questions, and updates relating to an event so that important planning conversations are retained with the event record.|
|Supporting Documents|Users can attach documents relevant to an event, such as programmes, floor plans, presentation requirements, or other supporting materials.|
|Venue Catalogue|The system maintains information about ConnectSphere venues, including location, capacity, facilities, accessibility, supported room layouts, operating hours, and other important characteristics.|
|Venue Availability Calendar|Authorised users can view when venues are available, tentatively held, confirmed, blocked, or otherwise unavailable.|
|Venue Search and Filtering|Event Coordinators can search for potential venues using requirements such as date, time, attendance, location, capacity, accessibility, supported layout, and required facilities.|
|Venue Suitability Checking|The system should assist users in identifying whether a venue appears suitable for an event. For example, a venue should not normally be treated as suitable when expected attendance exceeds its capacity.|
|Venue Booking Request|An Event Coordinator can request a venue for an event. The request contains the relevant event timing and venue requirements for Venue Staff to review.|
|Venue Booking Approval|Venue Staff can approve or reject a venue booking request and may provide a reason or suggest an alternative arrangement.|
|Tentative Venue Holding|Where permitted by ConnectSphere's business process, a venue may be temporarily held while an event is still being finalised. The rules governing tentative holds may differ from confirmed bookings.|
|Booking Conflict Detection|The system should identify incompatible or overlapping venue bookings and help prevent double-booking.|
|Setup and Turnaround Time|Venue availability may need to consider preparation before an event and reset time after an event, rather than only the published event start and end times.|

|**Functionality Area**|**Description**|
|---|---|
|Venue Unavailability Management|Venue Staff can block venues because of maintenance, renovation, safety issues, internal activities, or other operational reasons.|
|Room Layout Management|Event requirements may include layouts such as classroom, theatre, boardroom, banquet, exhibition, or another arrangement. Venue Staff can record which layouts are supported by each venue.|
|Event Capacity Management|Expected attendance and venue capacity should be considered throughout planning. A significant attendance change may require the suitability of an existing venue booking to be reviewed.|
|Equipment Catalogue|The system maintains information about equipment available for events, including type, description, quantity, location, and operational status.|
|Equipment Request Management|Event Coordinators can record equipment required for an event, including quantities and relevant technical requirements.|
|Equipment Availability Checking|Technical Support Staff can determine whether sufficient suitable equipment is available for the required date and time.|
|Equipment Reservation|Available equipment can be reserved for an event so that the same limited equipment is not simultaneously committed to incompatible events.|
|Equipment Maintenance Status|Equipment that is damaged, being repaired, or otherwise unavailable should not be treated as available for event use.|
|Technical Support Requests|Event Coordinators can indicate when an event requires technical support before or during the event and describe the support required.|
|Technical Staff Assignment|Where required, suitable Technical Support Staff can be allocated to support an event according to availability and event requirements.|
|Event Readiness Tracking|Event Coordinators can determine whether important arrangements such as venue, equipment, technical support, programme, and registration setup are ready.|
|Outstanding Action Tracking|The system can identify planning matters that are incomplete or require action before an event can be confirmed or delivered.|

|**Functionality Area**|**Description**|
|---|---|
|Event Confirmation|Once the necessary arrangements have been completed, the Event Coordinator can confirm the event. Confirmed arrangements should be visible to the appropriate users.|
|Attendee Registration|Where enabled, Attendees can register for confirmed events and provide the required registration information.|
|Registration Capacity|Registration may be limited according to the capacity defined for the event. The system should prevent or appropriately handle registrations beyond the permitted capacity.|
|Registration Period|An event may define when registration opens and closes. Attendees should only be able to register when registration is available.|
|Attendee Waiting List|Where supported, additional Attendees may join a waiting list when an event reaches capacity.|
|Registration Withdrawal|Attendees can withdraw their registration where permitted. The released place may subsequently become available to another Attendee.|
|Attendance Recording|ConnectSphere may record whether registered Attendees ultimately attended an event, allowing registration and attendance information to be distinguished.|
|Event Change Requests|Event Organisers can request permitted changes after an event has been submitted or confirmed. The Event Coordinator can review the requested change.|
|Impact of Event Changes|Significant changes, such as date, time, attendance, venue requirements, or equipment requirements, may require existing arrangements to be reviewed again.|
|Rescheduling|Events can be rescheduled where necessary. Existing venue, equipment, technical-support, and attendee arrangements may need to be reconsidered or updated.|
|Cancellation Management|An authorised user can cancel an event. Related venue and equipment reservations should no longer remain committed to a cancelled event, subject to the applicable business rules.|
|Notification System|Users can receive notifications about relevant events such as request submission, clarification requests, approval decisions, booking decisions, confirmation, changes, registration updates, or cancellation.|

|**Functionality Area**|**Description**|
|---|---|
|Reminder System|The system may remind relevant users about upcoming events, incomplete arrangements, registration deadlines, preparation activities, or other time-sensitive matters.|
|Event Calendar|Users can view appropriate upcoming events in calendar form. The information shown should depend on their role and access rights.|
|Search and Filtering|Users can search for events using suitable criteria such as event name, client organisation, date, venue, status, category, or assigned coordinator.|
|Activity History|Significant actions are recorded, including who performed the action and when it occurred, to support accountability and troubleshooting.|
|Change History|Users with appropriate access can review how important event information has changed over time.|
|Role-Based Dashboard|The system provides each internal or external role with an overview relevant to its responsibilities, such as events requiring attention, upcoming bookings, equipment requests, or attendee registrations.|
|Event Reports|Appropriate users can generate summaries containing event details, schedule, venue, operational requirements, registration information, and other relevant information.|
|Venue Usage Reports|Internal users can review venue bookings and usage over a selected period to support operational planning.|
|Registration Reports|Event Organisers and Event Coordinators can view or export attendee information where appropriate and subject to access restrictions.|
|Report Generation and Exporting|Suitable reports or event information can be exported into common formats for meetings, operational use, or record-keeping.|

**5. Typical event planning process**

Although events may differ, a typical event is expected to follow a process similar to the one below. The exact business rules for particular steps may be clarified during the customer Q&A sessions.

**Step 1 - Draft Event Request**: An Event Organiser creates a draft request containing the initial event requirements. They may save the request and continue editing it before submission.

**Step 2 - Submission**: The Event Organiser submits the request to ConnectSphere.

**Step 3 - Coordinator Assignment**: An Event Coordinator is assigned to the request and becomes the main ConnectSphere employee responsible for coordinating that event.

**Step 4 - Review and Clarification**: The Event Coordinator reviews the information provided. When information is incomplete or unclear, they request clarification or amendment from the Event Organiser.

**Step 5 - Initial Approval**: Once sufficient information is available, the Event Coordinator determines whether planning should proceed. Rejected or returned requests should retain an appropriate record of the decision.

**Step 6 - Venue Identification**: The Event Coordinator searches for venues that could satisfy the date, time, capacity, layout, accessibility, facilities, and setup requirements of the event.

**Step 7 - Venue Request**: The Event Coordinator submits a venue booking request. Venue Staff review the request and may approve it, reject it, or suggest another venue or arrangement.

**Step 8 - Technical Requirements**: Where equipment or technical support is required and requested by the Event Organiser, Technical Support Staff review the requirements and determine whether suitable resources can be provided and reserved.

**Step 9 - Event Preparation**: The Event Coordinator monitors outstanding arrangements. Venue Staff and Technical Support Staff update the relevant preparation information as work progresses.

**Step 10 - Event Confirmation**: When the essential arrangements have been completed, the Event Coordinator confirms the event. The Event Organiser can then view the confirmed arrangements.

**Step 11 - Attendee Registration**: Where registration is required, Attendees can register for the confirmed event during the permitted registration period and subject to the applicable capacity.

**Step 12 - Changes Before the Event**: The Event Organiser may subsequently request changes. The Event Coordinator determines whether those changes affect venue, equipment, technical-support, registration, or other arrangements.

**Step 13 - Event Delivery**: Venue Staff prepare the venue and Technical Support Staff prepare the necessary equipment or support. Relevant users should be able to access the latest confirmed information.

**Step 14 - Completion**: Once the event has taken place, it can be marked as completed. Relevant attendance information, operational notes, or issues may then be recorded and the event can be closed.

**6. Notifications**

Users should be kept informed when important events or arrangements relevant to them change. Notifications may be provided within the application or through another suitable communication channel.

Examples of situations that may generate a notification include:

A new event request is submitted.

An Event Coordinator is assigned.

Additional information or amendment is requested.

An event request is approved, rejected, or returned.

A venue booking is requested, approved, rejected, or changed.

Requested equipment is confirmed or found to be unavailable.

An event becomes confirmed.

The Event Organiser requests a significant change.

An event is rescheduled, postponed, or cancelled.

Registration opens or closes.

Registration reaches capacity or a waiting-list status changes.

A registered Attendee withdraws where that affects availability.

An upcoming event still has incomplete arrangements.

A venue or equipment availability change affects an upcoming event.

**7. Design**

The system should be both desktop- and mobile-friendly. External users may access the system from personal computers or mobile devices, while internal ConnectSphere staff may need access while preparing event spaces or equipment.

Information should be presented clearly and should not assume that users understand ConnectSphere's internal processes. The current status of an event, its confirmed arrangements, and any outstanding actions should be easy for the appropriate user to understand.

**8. Other requirements**

**a. Performance**

Common operations such as viewing an event, searching available venues, opening a venue calendar, checking equipment availability, or submitting a registration should complete within a reasonable time.

**b. Security**

The system should only allow authorised users to access protected information. Access should depend on the user's role and relationship to an event. For example, an Event Organiser should not normally be able to view events belonging to unrelated clients, and an Attendee should not be able to view internal planning information.

**c. Usability**

All groups of users should be able to complete their common activities without extensive training or guidance.

**d. Reliability and consistency**

The system should maintain consistent information when related event arrangements change. Users should not be presented with contradictory information regarding event dates, venue bookings, equipment availability, or registration status.

**e. Scalability**

The proposed solution should support ConnectSphere's anticipated growth over the next three years, including increases in events, users, client organisations, venues, equipment, and registrations.

**f. Auditability**

Important actions should be recorded. Where appropriate, ConnectSphere should be able to determine what was changed, who changed it, and when the change was made.

**g. Maintainability**

The organisation expects its processes to evolve over time. The proposed system should therefore be designed so that future functionality and business rules can be added without requiring the entire system to be rebuilt.

**_Notes:_**

The customer will continue to discuss the proposed system with Event Organisers, Event Coordinators, Venue Staff, Technical Support Staff, and other relevant stakeholders. There may be special cases and business rules that have not been described in this initial briefing.

Students are expected to use the scheduled customer Q&A sessions to clarify such matters and develop appropriate epics and user stories. The customer will subsequently identify the functionality considered most important for the first release.

The teaching team will release the exact project deliverables and grading rubrics in Week 4.

# Venue Booking

How [[connectsphere-event-services]] venues are catalogued, held, requested, approved, and protected from double-booking in the [[event-planning-venue-booking-system]]. Covers steps 6–7 of the planning process (see [[event-lifecycle]]). Assessment of whether a given venue *fits* an event is covered separately in [[venue-suitability]].

## Venue Catalogue

Venue Staff own venue master data (Source: customer-brief-no-1).

| Attribute | Notes |
|---|---|
| Location | Facility/site; all venues are owned and operated by ConnectSphere in Singapore |
| Capacity | Maximum attendance; drives suitability (see [[venue-suitability]]) |
| Facilities | e.g. video-conferencing, AV fit-out |
| Accessibility | Accessibility features of the space |
| Supported room layouts | classroom, theatre, boardroom, banquet, exhibition, other |
| Operating hours | Maintained by Venue Staff |
| Setup / teardown / turnaround time | Recorded **per venue** (#43) |

All venues are in Singapore and the system operates on Singapore time (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #36) — see [[non-functional-requirements]].

## Three-Slot Booking Model

Venues are booked in **three fixed daily time slots — AM, PM, Night**. A full-day booking is all three slots. Partial blocking (e.g. mornings only during a renovation) is expressed by blocking individual slots (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #50).

| Slot | Hours (as read) |
|---|---|
| AM | 7am – 12pm |
| PM | 1pm – 6pm |
| Night | 7pm – 12am |

> ⚠️ **Source ambiguity — slot labels.** The customer's answer to #50 reads verbatim: *"The venue will be booked based on 3 time slots (AM, PM, Night) if full day will be all 3 slots. AM (7am-12pm, 1pm-6pm, 7pm-12am)"*. Three time ranges are listed but only the **first** is labelled ("AM"). The table above applies the obvious positional mapping (AM / PM / Night in the order the slots were named), but this mapping is **inferred, not stated**. Note also the unbooked gaps at 12pm–1pm and 6pm–7pm, whose purpose (break, changeover, or a transcription slip) is not explained; they may or may not be intended to absorb setup and turnaround. Both points should be confirmed with the customer before the slot model is hard-coded.

**Team decision required:** the exact UX and implementation of slot selection are left open (#50) — including whether slots are stored as an enum or as concrete start/end timestamps, and how a multi-day or [[event-lifecycle|multi-session]] event maps onto slots.

## Booking Request and Approval

1. The Event Coordinator identifies candidate venues (search, filter, suitability check — see [[venue-suitability]]).
2. The Event Coordinator submits a **venue booking request** carrying the event timing and venue requirements (Source: customer-brief-no-1).
3. **Venue Staff** review and decide. They may approve, reject, or reject with a suggested alternative venue or arrangement (Source: customer-brief-no-1; is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #45).

Rejection with an alternative is **not** a formal counter-offer object in the system. Venue Staff suggest; **the Event Coordinator then makes the changes** and re-requests (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #45). This keeps the coordinator as the single point of control over event arrangements, consistent with [[event-request-workflow]].

Booking request, approval, rejection, and change are all notification triggers (see [[notifications]]).

## Tentative Holds

A venue may be temporarily held while an event is still being finalised (Source: customer-brief-no-1).

| Rule | Status |
|---|---|
| Only **one** active tentative hold *or* confirmed booking may exist for the same venue and overlapping time period | Specified (#41) |
| A tentative hold may later be confirmed or released | Specified (#41) |
| Hold duration / expiry period | **Not specified** (#39, #41) |
| Auto-release mechanism | **Not specified** (#39, #41) |
| Whether hold expiry is configurable | **Not specified** (#39) |

> **Team decision required:** expiry period and release mechanism for tentative holds are explicitly for the team to propose (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #39 and #41). This matters because a hold that never expires is functionally a confirmed booking and will silently block the venue — a stated pain point in the brief ("cancelled events may continue to occupy venue or equipment reservations").

Competing holds are therefore impossible by rule: the first hold wins the slot until it is confirmed or released. Multiple coordinators cannot shortlist the same slot in parallel.

## Conflict Detection and Double-Booking

The system must **identify and block** incompatible or overlapping bookings (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #35).

- This is a **hard block**, not a warning.
- The question explicitly offered a soft-warning-with-override option (override by Venue Staff for VIP organisations); the customer did **not** take it.
- No override or exception path for privileged clients is authorised. Any such path would need fresh clarification.

Overlap detection must account for setup and turnaround time, not only the published event start and end times (Source: customer-brief-no-1). See [[venue-suitability]] and [[event-readiness]].

## Setup and Turnaround Time

- Venue Staff record **setup, teardown and turnaround requirements per venue** (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #43).
- It is a per-venue attribute, not a global constant and not (currently) variable by event type or size.
- Insufficient turnaround between consecutive events is a named problem in the current manual process (Source: customer-brief-no-1).
- Extending an event may invalidate the turnaround before the next booking — a [[change-impact-management]] trigger.

Note the tension with the fixed three-slot model: if slots are indivisible, per-venue turnaround may be partly absorbed by the 12pm–1pm and 6pm–7pm gaps. Whether per-venue turnaround adds *on top of* slot boundaries is not stated and should be resolved by the team.

## Venue Unavailability and Blocking

- Venue Staff can block venues for maintenance, renovation, safety issues, internal activities, or other operational reasons (Source: customer-brief-no-1).
- Blocking is at slot granularity, enabling partial-day unavailability (#50).
- When a venue becomes unavailable **after** a booking is confirmed, Venue Staff are responsible for updating availability. The availability change affecting an upcoming event is a notification scenario, and **the Event Coordinator must then make the changes** (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #54).

> **Team decision required:** automation of the response to a post-confirmation venue loss (auto-release, auto-flag, auto-suggest alternatives) is for the team to propose (#54).

## Operating Hours

- Maintained by **Venue Staff** as part of venue information (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #46).
- **All days are treated as equal for now** — no day-of-week variation, no weekend/public-holiday distinction, no holiday calendar required (#46).

## Booking Horizon

- **No booking horizon has been specified** (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #57).
- **Team decision required:** propose one only if the solution requires it. Compare the parallel non-answers on event-request lead time (#78) and equipment/technical-support notice period (#25, see [[technical-support]]).

## Open Points Summary

| # | Question | Customer position |
|---|---|---|
| 50 | Slot definition | Three slots, AM/PM/Night; hours listed but labels garbled; UX for team |
| 41 | Concurrent holds | One active hold or confirmed booking per venue + overlapping period |
| 39 | Hold duration / auto-release | Not specified — **team to propose** |
| 35 | Double-booking | Hard block, no override |
| 45 | Rejection with alternative | Informal suggestion; coordinator makes the change |
| 43 | Turnaround | Per-venue, recorded by Venue Staff |
| 46 | Operating hours | Venue Staff maintain; all days equal |
| 54 | Post-confirmation unavailability | Venue Staff update; coordinator reacts; automation **team to propose** |
| 57 | Booking horizon | Not specified — **team to propose** |

See also [[open-questions]], [[user-roles]], [[access-control]], [[reporting]].

---
title: Venue Suitability
type: concept
sources:
  - Customer Brief no. 1.md
  - IS212 2026 Discussions Aug 26.md
  - IS212 2026 Discussions Aug 31.md
tags: [venue, suitability, search, filtering, capacity, room-layout, business-rules]
---

# Venue Suitability

Assessing whether a venue can satisfy an event's requirements. Distinct from the mechanics of holding and approving a booking, which are covered in [[venue-booking]].

## Search/Filtering vs Suitability Checking

The brief lists *Venue Search and Filtering* and *Venue Suitability Checking* as separate functionality areas without explaining the boundary. #83 asked whether filtering alone counts as the suitability check; the customer answered on 2026-08-31 that they are **two different functions** (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #83).

| | Search / Filtering | Suitability Checking |
|---|---|---|
| Purpose | **Narrow the list** of candidate venues | **Assess a selected or shortlisted venue** against current event requirements |
| Input | Criteria: date, time, capacity, accessibility, layout, facilities | The event's current requirements vs one venue's characteristics |
| Output | A list of potential venues | An indication of whether that venue can satisfy the event |
| Timing | Before selection | After a venue has been identified or selected |

> Filtering is used to narrow the list of venues based on criteria such as date, time, capacity, accessibility, layout, and facilities. Suitability checking evaluates whether a selected or shortlisted venue can satisfy the current event requirements. (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #83)

The two are not redundant: filtering answers *"which venues might work?"*; suitability answers *"does this venue still work?"* — a question that must be re-askable long after the search is over, because requirements change (see [[change-impact-management]]).

> **Team decision required:** presentation and implementation are explicitly left to the team (#83). The result "may be presented as an indication in the venue list or checked after selection" — i.e. an inline badge on search results, a check on selection, or both are all acceptable. The customer did not mandate a single UX.

## Suitability Factors

Drawn from the brief's list of factors on which venue suitability may depend (Source: customer-brief-no-1):

| Factor | Held on | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Proposed date and time | Event | Evaluated against existing bookings, holds, blocks — see [[venue-booking]] |
| Maximum capacity | Venue | Compared to expected attendance |
| Supported room layouts | Venue | Must include the requested layout |
| Accessibility | Venue | Must meet the event's stated accessibility requirements |
| Available facilities | Venue | e.g. video-conferencing for hybrid events |
| Existing bookings | Venue calendar | Overlapping bookings/holds are a hard block (#35) |
| Operating hours | Venue | Maintained by Venue Staff; all days equal for now (#46) |
| Setup requirements | Event + venue | Preparation before the published start time |
| Turnaround time | Venue | Reset time after the event; recorded per venue (#43) |
| Venue unavailability | Venue | Maintenance, renovation, safety restrictions, internal activity |

## Capacity vs Expected Attendance

- The brief's own worked example: *"a venue should not normally be treated as suitable when expected attendance exceeds its capacity"* (Source: customer-brief-no-1).
- The word **"normally"** is the customer's; it was not tightened in either discussion snapshot. Whether over-capacity is a hard block or an overridable warning is therefore **unresolved**. Contrast [[venue-booking]] #35, where double-booking was explicitly confirmed as a hard block — no equivalent statement exists for capacity.
- Expected attendance and venue capacity are to be considered **throughout planning**, not only at initial selection (Source: customer-brief-no-1, *Event Capacity Management*).
- The brief's canonical impact example: raising attendance from 80 to 150 may make the already-selected venue unsuitable.
- Registration capacity is a related but separate limit — see [[attendee-registration]].

> **Team decision required:** whether exceeding capacity blocks a booking outright or raises an overridable warning, and who (if anyone) may override.

## Supported Room Layouts

- Event requirements may specify classroom, theatre, boardroom, banquet, exhibition, or another arrangement (Source: customer-brief-no-1).
- **Venue Staff record which layouts each venue supports** (Source: customer-brief-no-1, *Room Layout Management*).
- Layout is both a filter criterion and a suitability criterion (#83 lists it in both).
- Layout interacts with capacity: the same room seats different numbers under theatre vs banquet layout. The brief models capacity as a single venue attribute and does **not** state whether capacity varies by layout. This is a modelling gap for the team.

## Accessibility and Facilities

- Accessibility requirements are supplied by the Event Organiser at request time (Source: customer-brief-no-1) — see [[event-request-workflow]].
- Facilities requirements are frequently under-specified by organisers. The brief's example: an organiser requests a hybrid event without explaining what video-conferencing facilities are required; resolving this is the Event Coordinator's clarification duty (Step 4). The equivalent clarification path for equipment runs through the coordinator too — see [[technical-support]].

## Re-triggering Suitability

#83 asked explicitly whether the check should re-trigger on venue search, on coordinator submission, on updated event requirements, or all. The answer defined the two functions but did not enumerate trigger points, so the trigger set is inferred from the surrounding rules:

| Moment | Basis |
|---|---|
| On selecting/shortlisting a venue | #83 — suitability assesses a venue "after it has been identified or selected" |
| On submitting a venue booking request | Brief: the request carries "the relevant event timing and venue requirements for Venue Staff to review" |
| On a significant change to event requirements | #4 — changes to date/time, attendance, venue requirements are significant and "may invalidate confirmed arrangements"; #8 — changes may occur even after confirmation and require affected arrangements to be reviewed again |
| On a change to the venue itself | #54 — Venue Staff update availability; the coordinator must react |
| On reschedule / postponement with a new date | #16, #69 — arrangements must be reviewed again |

Significant changes requiring re-evaluation are handled under [[change-impact-management]]; outstanding arrangements roll up into [[event-readiness]].

> **Team decision required:** the exact trigger points and whether re-evaluation is automatic or coordinator-initiated. The customer said only that "the exact implementation is for you to propose" (#4) and gave no trigger list in #83.

## Snapshot Note

#83 does **not** appear in the Aug 26 snapshot (it was posted 2026-08-27 and answered 2026-08-31). The search/suitability distinction is therefore new information in [[is212-discussions-2026-08-31]] and supersedes any earlier assumption that filtering alone was sufficient.

See also [[venue-booking]], [[open-questions]], [[user-roles]], [[reporting]].

---
title: Equipment Management
type: concept
sources:
  - Customer Brief no. 1.md
  - IS212 2026 Discussions Aug 26.md
  - IS212 2026 Discussions Aug 31.md
tags: [equipment, inventory, availability, reservation, maintenance, business-rules]
---

# Equipment Management

Catalogue, availability, reservation, and condition tracking for ConnectSphere's event equipment. The staffing and review side of the same workflow is covered in [[technical-support]].

## Equipment Catalogue

The system maintains equipment records with (Source: customer-brief-no-1):

| Attribute | Notes |
|---|---|
| Type | e.g. projector, microphone, VC unit |
| Description | Free-form detail / technical specification |
| Quantity | Must be known to the system (#13) |
| Location | Equipment has a **physical location** (#2) |
| Operational status | Available, unavailable, damaged, under maintenance (#23) |

## Availability: Two Rules That Coexist

Two separate rules constrain when a piece of equipment can be committed to an event. They govern **different ends** of the event.

> ⚠️ **Contradiction (raised, then resolved).** On 2026-08-28 the team flagged #2 ("transfer and preparation time should be considered when determining availability") as apparently contradicting #5 ("equipment is returned to ConnectSphere for assessment and is only available again from Return Day + 1"), and asked which workflow stands. The customer resolved this on 2026-08-31: **both rules apply, at different points in the equipment lifecycle. They are not alternatives to each other.** (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #2 follow-up)

| Rule | Governs | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Transfer and preparation time from the equipment's current location to the event venue must be considered | **Pre-event** availability | #2 |
| Equipment may be collected from **D-1**; after return and inspection it is available again only from **Return Day + 1** | **Post-event** availability | #5, restated in #2 follow-up |

### Lifecycle Chain

As given verbatim by the customer (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #2 follow-up, 2026-08-31):

```
Current equipment location
→ transfer/preparation to event venue
→ D-1 collection / event commitment period
→ event use
→ return to ConnectSphere
→ inspection/preparation
→ available again from Return Day +1
```

Note the return leg: equipment goes back **to ConnectSphere** for inspection, not directly to the next venue. Transfer time is therefore consumed on the outbound leg of every reservation, measured from wherever the item currently sits.

> **Team decision required:** "How the system represents transfer time, preparation time and the equipment's current location is for the solution team to propose" (#2). Options include a per-item location field with a transfer-duration matrix, a flat buffer, or folding transfer into the D-1 window.

### Snapshot Note

In the Aug 26 snapshot, #2 was **answered** with only the transfer-time rule and no reconciliation with #5. The apparent conflict was raised as a follow-up on 2026-08-28, which re-opened the question, and was resolved 2026-08-31. The Aug 31 snapshot still lists #2 under *Unanswered* because it was re-opened by that follow-up, even though the follow-up itself contains the resolution. Cite [[is212-discussions-2026-08-31]] for the reconciled rule.

## No Same-Day Sharing

A single piece of equipment **cannot** be shared between two events on the same day (e.g. a morning event and an afternoon event) (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #5).

This follows directly from the D-1 / Return Day +1 rule: the effective commitment window for one event spans at minimum from D-1 through Return Day +1, which necessarily swallows any other same-day event. The practical consequence for the [[venue-booking]] three-slot model is that equipment does **not** follow venue slot granularity — a venue can host AM, PM, and Night events on one day, but the same projector cannot serve all three.

## Reservation Rules

| Rule | Position |
|---|---|
| Maximum reservation period | **None** (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #82) |
| Minimum reservation period | Not stated; #82 asked about both max and min, and only the maximum was answered |
| Minimum notice period for equipment requests | **Not specified** — team to propose (#25); see [[technical-support]] |
| Partial reservation when only some items are available | **Allowed** (#90) |
| Effect of a reschedule on existing reservations | Arrangement must be reviewed again; workflow for the team to propose (#16) — see [[change-impact-management]] |

**Snapshot note:** #82 was **unanswered** in the Aug 26 snapshot and answered on 2026-08-31 with "No maximum reservation period." Any backlog item written before that date against #82 should be revisited.

### Partial Reservation

Technical Support Staff may reserve the equipment that is available and suitable even when other requested items are unavailable. They should identify which requirements can be fulfilled and highlight unavailable items or suggest alternatives. **The Event Coordinator then determines whether the outstanding requirement affects overall event readiness** (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #90).

Implication: an equipment requirement is not atomic. Its fulfilment state is per-line-item, and the roll-up to "ready / not ready" is a coordinator judgement, not a system computation — see [[event-readiness]].

## Pooled vs Serialised Modelling

- The customer declined to prescribe whether equipment is tracked as individually serialised items or as a pooled quantity counter (#13).
- The single binding constraint: **"the system needs to know the quantity of equipment available"** (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #13).

> **Team decision required:** pooled vs serialised inventory modelling. This choice is load-bearing — the D-1 / Return Day +1 rule and the per-item **location** and **operational status** attributes (#2, #23) all imply per-item state, which is awkward to express against a bare pooled counter. A pooled model would need per-unit sub-state to satisfy #2 and #23 anyway.

## Maintenance, Damage, and Defect Logging

- **Technical Support Staff are responsible for maintaining equipment status** (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #9). Event Coordinators do not set it. See [[user-roles]] and [[access-control]].
- Equipment can be recorded as unavailable, damaged, or under maintenance (#23).
- Equipment that is damaged, being repaired, or otherwise unavailable must **not** be treated as available for event use (Source: customer-brief-no-1).
- On return, Technical Support Staff can record **defects, damage, missing items, or other issues**, and the operational status of the affected item is updated accordingly (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #86).
- Reserved equipment becoming unavailable through damage or maintenance is an explicit change-impact scenario in the brief and a [[notifications]] trigger.

### Not in Scope

| Item | Position |
|---|---|
| Expected return date field for equipment under maintenance | **Not specified** — team may propose (#23) |
| Automatic flagging / pre-booking when equipment returns to service | **Not specified** — team may propose (#23) |
| Full equipment maintenance workflow | Not listed as a functional requirement; recorded by the customer as a *consideration* only (#23) |
| Post-event equipment health checklist | **Kept outside the system** — "we do not need to keep track in the system" (#85) |

The #85 answer draws a clear scope boundary: the *outcome* of the post-event assessment (defect, damage, status change) is recorded in the system per #86, but the **checklist instrument itself is not modelled**. Do not build checklist templates or per-item inspection forms.

## Open Points Summary

| # | Question | Customer position |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | Equipment location / transit downtime | Location exists; transfer + prep time affects pre-event availability; representation **team to propose** |
| 5 | Same-day sharing | Not allowed; D-1 collection, available again Return Day +1 |
| 9 | Who sets damaged/unavailable | Technical Support Staff |
| 13 | Pooled vs serialised | **Team to propose**; quantity must be known |
| 16 | Reschedule effect | Re-review required; workflow **team to propose** |
| 23 | Maintenance return date / pre-booking | Not specified; maintenance workflow not a requirement |
| 82 | Max reservation period | None (answered 2026-08-31; unanswered in Aug 26 snapshot) |
| 85 | Post-event health checklist | Outside the system |
| 86 | Defect logging on return | Supported; status updated accordingly |
| 90 | Partial reservation | Allowed; coordinator judges readiness impact |

See also [[technical-support]], [[event-readiness]], [[change-impact-management]], [[open-questions]].

---
title: Technical Support
type: concept
sources:
  - Customer Brief no. 1.md
  - IS212 2026 Discussions Aug 26.md
  - IS212 2026 Discussions Aug 31.md
tags: [technical-support, staffing, rostering, equipment, roles, business-rules]

# Technical Support

The Technical Support Staff role: reviewing equipment and technical requirements, reserving resources, and being assigned to support events on-site. The equipment inventory and availability rules themselves are in [[equipment-management]].

## Responsibilities

Technical Support Staff are internal users responsible for equipment, technical requirements, equipment reservations, and technical support for events (Source: customer-brief-no-1). Concretely:

| Responsibility | Source |
|---|---|
| Maintain records of available equipment | customer-brief-no-1 |
| Maintain equipment operational status (damaged, under maintenance, unavailable) | #9, #23 |
| Determine whether sufficient suitable equipment can be reserved for a date and time | customer-brief-no-1 |
| Reserve available and suitable equipment against an event | #19, #90 |
| Record questions, comments, or clarification needs against an event | #87 |
| Log defects, damage, or missing items on equipment return | #86 |
| Be assigned to support an event on-site | customer-brief-no-1, #88, #89 |
| Update preparation information as work progresses (Step 9, Step 13) | customer-brief-no-1 |

Access is **not** scoped by venue, equipment type, or location — Technical Support Staff have access to the information needed for their responsibilities organisation-wide (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #66). See [[access-control]] and [[user-roles]].

## Equipment Requirement Review Flow

Step 8 of the planning process (Source: customer-brief-no-1). The flow is deliberately **lighter than venue booking**:

1. The **Event Coordinator records the equipment requirement** for the event, including quantities and relevant technical requirements.
2. **Technical Support Staff review** whether the requested equipment is suitable and available.
3. Available equipment **can then be reserved** for the event.

> There is **no formal request → approval workflow** for equipment equivalent to the venue booking approval in [[venue-booking]]. The customer answered #19 directly: the coordinator records the requirement, TSS review suitability and availability, and available equipment is reserved. (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #19)

Practical consequence: there is no "approved"/"rejected" decision object for equipment. The outcome is expressed as reservation state plus flagged unavailable items. Requested equipment being confirmed or found unavailable is still a [[notifications]] trigger (Source: customer-brief-no-1).

Reservation may be **partial** — suitable available items are reserved even while others are unavailable, with the unavailable items highlighted or alternatives suggested; the Event Coordinator then judges the impact on overall readiness (#90). See [[event-readiness]].

## Clarification of Insufficient Information

When an event's technical requirements are incomplete or unclear (the brief's example: a hybrid event requested without specifying video-conferencing needs), the flow is (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #87):

1. Technical Support Staff **record questions, comments, or clarification needs against the event**.
2. Where clarification from the **Event Organiser** is required, the **Event Coordinator remains the main liaison** and coordinates the response.
3. The clarification and its response are **retained with the event record**.

Technical Support Staff therefore do **not** contact the Event Organiser directly. The coordinator's role as sole external liaison, established in the brief and in [[event-request-workflow]], holds for technical clarifications too. This mirrors [[venue-booking]] #45, where Venue Staff suggest an alternative but the coordinator makes the change.

Comments are retained with the event record; whether they are threaded or flat is a UI/UX decision (#15).

## Technical Support Requests

- Event Coordinators can indicate when an event requires technical support **before or during** the event and describe the support required (Source: customer-brief-no-1).
- Technical support is one of the arrangements that may be **essential** for a given event — and if essential and incomplete, the event must not be confirmable (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #80). There is no fixed list of essential arrangements; it depends on the event (see [[event-readiness]]).
- Insufficient notice to Technical Support Staff about upcoming equipment or support requirements is a named pain point in the current manual process (Source: customer-brief-no-1) — yet no minimum notice period was set (see below).

## Staff Assignment and Rostering

| Question | Customer position | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Can staff self-declare availability for rostering? | **No.** No separate staff self-declaration of availability is currently required. The system only needs to maintain **sufficient availability information to support staff assignment**. | #89 |
| How is availability maintained? | **Team decision required** — "How availability is maintained can be proposed by students." | #89 |
| How often is the roster updated? | **No fixed roster update frequency is required.** | #88 |
| Who does the rostering — system-assigned or manual? | **No hard requirement** either way. | #88 |
| Minimum notice period for equipment / technical support requests | **None specified** — team to propose if the solution requires one. | #25 |

> **Team decision required (three related items):** #88 and #89 together leave the entire staff-assignment mechanism open — availability representation, assignment method (manual vs automated), and update cadence. The only fixed constraint is that *enough* availability information must exist to make an assignment possible. A minimal design (coordinator or TSS lead picks a name, no availability calendar) satisfies the letter of both answers.

Contrast the coordinator side, where assignment **is** specified: an Event Operations Manager assigns and reassigns Event Coordinators, with no acceptance step and no in-system approval (#73, #94, #95). No equivalent manager role was named for Technical Support Staff. Whether the Event Operations Manager, the Event Coordinator, or a TSS lead performs technical staffing is **not stated** and is an [[open-questions]] item.

A person may hold multiple roles (#56), so a Technical Support Staff member can also be, for example, an Attendee at another event.

## Notice Period

- **No minimum notice period has been specified** for equipment and technical support requests (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #25).
- **Team decision required:** propose an appropriate approach if the solution requires one.
- This sits alongside two other unset time bounds: no minimum event-request lead time (#78) and no venue booking horizon (#57, see [[venue-booking]]). If the team introduces one lead-time rule, the three should be designed consistently.

## Open Points Summary

| # | Question | Customer position |
|---|---|---|
| 19 | Formal equipment approval workflow? | No — record requirement, TSS review, reserve |
| 87 | Clarifying insufficient technical info | TSS record against event; Event Coordinator liaises with organiser; retain with record |
| 88 | Roster frequency / who rosters | No fixed frequency; no hard requirement system vs manual |
| 89 | Staff self-declared availability | Not required; availability representation **team to propose** |
| 25 | Minimum notice period | None specified — **team to propose** |
| 90 | Partial fulfilment | TSS reserve what's available, flag the rest; coordinator judges readiness |
| 66 | Scope of staff access | Organisation-wide, not scoped by venue/equipment type/location |

See also [[equipment-management]], [[event-readiness]], [[user-roles]], [[event-lifecycle]].

1	# Wiki — Schema
2	
3	This file defines the conventions and workflows for maintaining the PM Intern Learning wiki.
4	
5	## Architecture
6	
7	- **`raw/`** — Immutable source documents. Never modify these. This is the source of truth.
8	- **`wiki/`** — LLM-generated markdown pages. The LLM owns this layer entirely.
9	  - `wiki/sources/` — One summary page per ingested source document.
10	  - `wiki/concepts/` — Pages for key ideas, frameworks, and methodologies.
11	  - `wiki/entities/` — Pages for organizations, products, and people.
12	- **`index.md`** — Content catalog of every wiki page, organized by category.
13	- **`log.md`** — Chronological append-only record of wiki activity.
14	
15	## Conventions
16	
17	- **Links**: Use Obsidian-style `[[wikilinks]]` for all cross-references between wiki pages. Use the page's filename without extension (e.g. `[[decision-making]]`).
18	- **Frontmatter**: Every wiki page has YAML frontmatter with `title`, `type` (source-summary | concept | entity), `sources` (list of raw files this page draws from), and `tags`.
19	- **Citations**: When a claim comes from a specific source, note it inline, e.g. `(Source: pm-intern-learning)`.
20	- **Tone**: Concise, structured, third-person. Use headers, bullet points, and tables. Avoid fluff.
21	- **Contradictions**: If a new source contradicts an existing wiki page, flag it explicitly with a `> ⚠️ Contradiction:` callout.
22	
23	## Workflows
24	
25	### Ingest a new source
26	1. Place the source document in `raw/`.
27	2. Read the source fully.
28	3. Create a source summary page in `wiki/sources/`.
29	4. Create or update concept pages in `wiki/concepts/` for each major topic.
30	5. Create or update entity pages in `wiki/entities/` for organizations, products, people.
31	6. Update `wiki/index.md` with new/changed pages.
32	7. Append an entry to `wiki/log.md`.
33	
34	### Query
35	1. Read `wiki/index.md` to find relevant pages.
36	2. Read those pages and synthesize an answer.
37	3. If the answer is worth preserving, file it as a new wiki page.
38	
39	### Lint
40	1. Check for orphan pages (no inbound links).
41	2. Check for missing pages (referenced but don't exist).
42	3. Check for stale information superseded by newer sources.
43	4. Check for missing cross-references between related pages.
44	5. Suggest new sources or questions to investigate.
