**IS212 (AY 2026/27 T1) – Customer Briefing**

**** Please Read This First ****

For the IS212 project, you will build the first release of a system using the scrum process.

In this document, you will find a briefing from the (mock) customer describing their desired system.

Please note that -

This customer briefing is (initially) **deliberately ambiguous. Why?** No real-world customer knows _precisely_ what they want on day 1, and there may be edge cases or conflicting expectations that have not yet been considered.

You can disambiguate the briefing by 'meeting' the customer (role played by your section's instructor) during the scheduled Q&A sessions over the next few weeks. Questions through other channels will not be answered.

**Each section has a different 'customer'.** Please only consider clarifications provided by your section's customer, as clarifications in other sections may not be consistent.

The customer briefing is quite wide-ranging. Don't panic! You will NOT build the entire system. The customer **will eventually clarify the core functionalities to cover in your first release** (i.e., your Week 12 submission). Wait for these to be identified in Week 4 before you start coding, and work on creating epics/user stories for your product backlog in the meantime.

The IS212 project instructions will be released on Friday, Week 3 (6pm). These instructions will list the artefacts expected in your submission and the grading rubrics, which emphasise the **scrum process, requirements discovery, software quality, and your documentation of these activities** more than the final product alone.

Until the project instructions are released, use Weeks 2-4 to understand the customer's needs and translate them into a product backlog of epics and user stories. We do not recommend sprinting until Week 4, especially as the customer has not yet identified the core functionalities to be implemented in the first release.

  

**Customer Briefing: Event Planning and Venue Booking System**

**1. Organisation**

ConnectSphere Event Services is a regional organisation that provides professional event planning and venue services to organisations across Southeast Asia. The company organises a wide variety of events, such as conferences, seminars, workshops, etc.

It operates and owns several event facilities within Singapore. ConnectSphere also maintains equipment and supporting resources commonly required for events. ConnectSphere currently has approximately 500 staff for its operations, taking on the role of **Event Coordinators**, **Venue Staff**, and **Technical Support Staff**.

As the organization expands, the number of events, venues, resources, clients, and participants that must be coordinated has increased significantly. ConnectSphere would therefore like to modernise the way it manages its events.

The proposed system will be used by internal and external users.

**2. Background**

ConnectSphere currently relies on a mixture of email, spreadsheets, shared calendars, messaging applications, online forms, and manually maintained documents to organise events. Information for a single event may therefore be spread across several places and managed by different employees.

A typical event begins when an external **Event Organiser** approaches ConnectSphere with an event to host or support. The Event Organiser is responsible for providing the initial requirements and communicating with ConnectSphere about the event, and provides preliminary information such as the purpose and type of event, preferred date and time, expected number of attendees, general programme, room-layout preferences, accessibility requirements, equipment requirements, registration requirements, and any other special arrangements.

An **Event Coordinator** is then assigned to the request and acts as the main liaison for the Event Organiser, who will review the request and contact the Event Organiser for any clarifications and coordination before confirmation.

For example, the Event Organiser may request a "large room" without specifying the expected attendance or may request a hybrid event without explaining what video-conferencing facilities are required.

Once the basic requirements are sufficiently clear, the Event Coordinator works with **Venue Staff** to identify a suitable venue. Venue Staff maintain information about ConnectSphere's rooms and spaces and are responsible for deciding whether the requested venue can be made available for the event.

Venue suitability may depend on several factors, such as the proposed date and time, maximum capacity, supported room layouts, accessibility, available facilities, existing bookings, operating hours, setup requirements, and the turnaround time required between consecutive events. A venue may also be unavailable because of maintenance, renovation, safety restrictions, or another internal activity.

Some events also require technical equipment and support. In these cases, **Technical Support Staff** review the requested equipment and technical support. They maintain records of available equipment, determine whether sufficient equipment can be reserved, and may also be assigned to support an event on-site.

Equipment may already be reserved for another event, located at another venue, damaged, or undergoing maintenance. The planning process may therefore involve several rounds of communication before an event can be confirmed.

Once the essential arrangements have been made, the Event Coordinator can confirm the event with the Event Organiser. For events that require registration, Attendees may subsequently register through the system and receive the event information.

Changes frequently occur after an event has been proposed or even after it has been confirmed. For example:

·       The Event Organiser may request a different date or time.

·       Expected attendance may increase or decrease.

·       Additional equipment or technical support may be requested.

·       The programme may be extended, shortened, or split into multiple sessions.

·       A booked venue may become unavailable because of an operational issue.

·       Reserved equipment may become unavailable because of damage or maintenance.

·       The Event Organiser may postpone or cancel the event due to unforeseen circumstances.

·       Registration numbers may reach the event capacity earlier than expected.

Such changes can affect arrangements that have already been made. Increasing attendance from 80 to 150 people may make the selected venue unsuitable. Changing an event date may create a venue or equipment conflict. Extending an event may affect the turnaround time needed before another booking. ConnectSphere therefore expects the proposed system to help users identify and manage these relationships.

The current process creates several difficulties:

·       Event requests may be incomplete, duplicated, or difficult to track.

·       Event Coordinators may maintain separate spreadsheets or personal notes, creating different versions of the same event information.

·       Event Organisers may be unsure whether an event, venue, or equipment arrangement has been approved or confirmed.

·       Venue Staff may receive incomplete or outdated event requirements.

·       The same venue or equipment may accidentally be considered available for more than one event.

·       Insufficient setup or turnaround time may be left between consecutive events.

·       Last-minute changes may not reach all affected staff or attendees.

·       Cancelled events may continue to occupy venue or equipment reservations.

·       Technical Support Staff may receive insufficient notice about upcoming equipment or support requirements.

·       Attendees may receive outdated dates, times, or venue information after an event changes.

·       It is difficult to identify which upcoming events still have incomplete arrangements.

·       It is difficult to determine who changed important event information and when the change occurred.

ConnectSphere would therefore like to develop a custom-built Event Planning and Venue Booking System that provides a single platform for its processes.

**3. Target group of users**

The system will be used by ConnectSphere and external users. The roles below are the roles referred to throughout this customer briefing.

|**Role**|**Internal / External**|**Main Responsibility**|
|---|---|---|
|Event Organiser|External|Client representative who has an event to organize and communicates event requirements to ConnectSphere.|
|Event Coordinator|Internal|They are assigned to coordinate the overall planning of an event and act as the main internal point of contact.|
|Venue Staff|Internal|They are responsible for venue information, availability, booking decisions, and physical venue preparation.|
|Technical Support Staff|Internal|They are responsible for equipment, technical requirements, equipment reservations, and technical support for events.|
|Attendee|External|Participant who registers for and attends an event.|

**4. Application features**

The following describes the broad functionality ConnectSphere is considering for the proposed system. The customer briefing is intentionally wide-ranging, and the first software release may not implement every functionality described below.

|**Functionality Area**|**Description**|
|---|---|
|User Authorisation and Authentication|Allow users to securely access the system. Access to information and functionality depends on whether the user is an Event Organiser, Event Coordinator, Venue Staff member, Technical Support Staff member, or Attendee.|
|User Profile Management|Users can maintain relevant profile information such as name, organisation, contact details, and communication preferences. Internal users may also have information relating to their department or responsibilities.|
|Client Management|ConnectSphere can maintain information about external client organisations. Multiple Event Organisers may belong to the same organisation, and an organisation may have several past and upcoming events.|
|Event Request Creation|Event Organisers can create event requests containing information such as the event name, description, purpose, preferred dates, expected attendance, venue requirements, accessibility needs, and other planning information.|
|Draft Event Requests|Event Organisers can save an event request before submission so that incomplete information can be completed or reviewed later.|
|Event Categories|Events can be classified into categories such as conference, workshop, training session, exhibition, meeting, seminar, networking event, or any other type defined by ConnectSphere.|
|Event Review and Approval|Event Coordinators can review submitted requests, request amendments or clarification, approve requests, or reject requests where appropriate.|
|Coordinator Assignment|Events can be assigned to an Event Coordinator responsible for managing the planning process. Reassignment may be required when staff responsibilities or availability change.|
|Event Status Management|Events progress through suitable statuses so that users can understand their current stage, for example draft, submitted, under review, approved, planning, awaiting arrangements, confirmed, completed, cancelled, or rejected.|
|Event Information Management|Authorised users can update relevant event information during planning. The system should distinguish between ordinary edits and changes that may affect arrangements already confirmed.|
|Event Programme and Agenda|Event Organisers or Event Coordinators can record the programme for an event, including sessions, breaks, presentations, or other scheduled activities.|
|Multi-Session Events|Some events may contain several sessions within the same day or across multiple days. Sessions may have different timings or operational requirements.|

|**Functionality Area**|**Description**|
|---|---|
|Recurring or Similar Events|Where useful, information from a previous or recurring event may be reused to reduce repeated data entry, while still allowing the new event to have different dates and requirements.|
|Comments and Discussion|Event Organisers and relevant internal users can exchange comments, questions, and updates relating to an event so that important planning conversations are retained with the event record.|
|Supporting Documents|Users can attach documents relevant to an event, such as programmes, floor plans, presentation requirements, or other supporting materials.|
|Venue Catalogue|The system maintains information about ConnectSphere venues, including location, capacity, facilities, accessibility, supported room layouts, operating hours, and other important characteristics.|
|Venue Availability Calendar|Authorised users can view when venues are available, tentatively held, confirmed, blocked, or otherwise unavailable.|
|Venue Search and Filtering|Event Coordinators can search for potential venues using requirements such as date, time, attendance, location, capacity, accessibility, supported layout, and required facilities.|
|Venue Suitability Checking|The system should assist users in identifying whether a venue appears suitable for an event. For example, a venue should not normally be treated as suitable when expected attendance exceeds its capacity.|
|Venue Booking Request|An Event Coordinator can request a venue for an event. The request contains the relevant event timing and venue requirements for Venue Staff to review.|
|Venue Booking Approval|Venue Staff can approve or reject a venue booking request and may provide a reason or suggest an alternative arrangement.|
|Tentative Venue Holding|Where permitted by ConnectSphere's business process, a venue may be temporarily held while an event is still being finalised. The rules governing tentative holds may differ from confirmed bookings.|
|Booking Conflict Detection|The system should identify incompatible or overlapping venue bookings and help prevent double-booking.|
|Setup and Turnaround Time|Venue availability may need to consider preparation before an event and reset time after an event, rather than only the published event start and end times.|

|**Functionality Area**|**Description**|
|---|---|
|Venue Unavailability Management|Venue Staff can block venues because of maintenance, renovation, safety issues, internal activities, or other operational reasons.|
|Room Layout Management|Event requirements may include layouts such as classroom, theatre, boardroom, banquet, exhibition, or another arrangement. Venue Staff can record which layouts are supported by each venue.|
|Event Capacity Management|Expected attendance and venue capacity should be considered throughout planning. A significant attendance change may require the suitability of an existing venue booking to be reviewed.|
|Equipment Catalogue|The system maintains information about equipment available for events, including type, description, quantity, location, and operational status.|
|Equipment Request Management|Event Coordinators can record equipment required for an event, including quantities and relevant technical requirements.|
|Equipment Availability Checking|Technical Support Staff can determine whether sufficient suitable equipment is available for the required date and time.|
|Equipment Reservation|Available equipment can be reserved for an event so that the same limited equipment is not simultaneously committed to incompatible events.|
|Equipment Maintenance Status|Equipment that is damaged, being repaired, or otherwise unavailable should not be treated as available for event use.|
|Technical Support Requests|Event Coordinators can indicate when an event requires technical support before or during the event and describe the support required.|
|Technical Staff Assignment|Where required, suitable Technical Support Staff can be allocated to support an event according to availability and event requirements.|
|Event Readiness Tracking|Event Coordinators can determine whether important arrangements such as venue, equipment, technical support, programme, and registration setup are ready.|
|Outstanding Action Tracking|The system can identify planning matters that are incomplete or require action before an event can be confirmed or delivered.|

|**Functionality Area**|**Description**|
|---|---|
|Event Confirmation|Once the necessary arrangements have been completed, the Event Coordinator can confirm the event. Confirmed arrangements should be visible to the appropriate users.|
|Attendee Registration|Where enabled, Attendees can register for confirmed events and provide the required registration information.|
|Registration Capacity|Registration may be limited according to the capacity defined for the event. The system should prevent or appropriately handle registrations beyond the permitted capacity.|
|Registration Period|An event may define when registration opens and closes. Attendees should only be able to register when registration is available.|
|Attendee Waiting List|Where supported, additional Attendees may join a waiting list when an event reaches capacity.|
|Registration Withdrawal|Attendees can withdraw their registration where permitted. The released place may subsequently become available to another Attendee.|
|Attendance Recording|ConnectSphere may record whether registered Attendees ultimately attended an event, allowing registration and attendance information to be distinguished.|
|Event Change Requests|Event Organisers can request permitted changes after an event has been submitted or confirmed. The Event Coordinator can review the requested change.|
|Impact of Event Changes|Significant changes, such as date, time, attendance, venue requirements, or equipment requirements, may require existing arrangements to be reviewed again.|
|Rescheduling|Events can be rescheduled where necessary. Existing venue, equipment, technical-support, and attendee arrangements may need to be reconsidered or updated.|
|Cancellation Management|An authorised user can cancel an event. Related venue and equipment reservations should no longer remain committed to a cancelled event, subject to the applicable business rules.|
|Notification System|Users can receive notifications about relevant events such as request submission, clarification requests, approval decisions, booking decisions, confirmation, changes, registration updates, or cancellation.|

|**Functionality Area**|**Description**|
|---|---|
|Reminder System|The system may remind relevant users about upcoming events, incomplete arrangements, registration deadlines, preparation activities, or other time-sensitive matters.|
|Event Calendar|Users can view appropriate upcoming events in calendar form. The information shown should depend on their role and access rights.|
|Search and Filtering|Users can search for events using suitable criteria such as event name, client organisation, date, venue, status, category, or assigned coordinator.|
|Activity History|Significant actions are recorded, including who performed the action and when it occurred, to support accountability and troubleshooting.|
|Change History|Users with appropriate access can review how important event information has changed over time.|
|Role-Based Dashboard|The system provides each internal or external role with an overview relevant to its responsibilities, such as events requiring attention, upcoming bookings, equipment requests, or attendee registrations.|
|Event Reports|Appropriate users can generate summaries containing event details, schedule, venue, operational requirements, registration information, and other relevant information.|
|Venue Usage Reports|Internal users can review venue bookings and usage over a selected period to support operational planning.|
|Registration Reports|Event Organisers and Event Coordinators can view or export attendee information where appropriate and subject to access restrictions.|
|Report Generation and Exporting|Suitable reports or event information can be exported into common formats for meetings, operational use, or record-keeping.|

**5. Typical event planning process**

Although events may differ, a typical event is expected to follow a process similar to the one below. The exact business rules for particular steps may be clarified during the customer Q&A sessions.

**Step 1 - Draft Event Request**: An Event Organiser creates a draft request containing the initial event requirements. They may save the request and continue editing it before submission.

**Step 2 - Submission**: The Event Organiser submits the request to ConnectSphere.

**Step 3 - Coordinator Assignment**: An Event Coordinator is assigned to the request and becomes the main ConnectSphere employee responsible for coordinating that event.

**Step 4 - Review and Clarification**: The Event Coordinator reviews the information provided. When information is incomplete or unclear, they request clarification or amendment from the Event Organiser.

**Step 5 - Initial Approval**: Once sufficient information is available, the Event Coordinator determines whether planning should proceed. Rejected or returned requests should retain an appropriate record of the decision.

**Step 6 - Venue Identification**: The Event Coordinator searches for venues that could satisfy the date, time, capacity, layout, accessibility, facilities, and setup requirements of the event.

**Step 7 - Venue Request**: The Event Coordinator submits a venue booking request. Venue Staff review the request and may approve it, reject it, or suggest another venue or arrangement.

**Step 8 - Technical Requirements**: Where equipment or technical support is required and requested by the Event Organiser, Technical Support Staff review the requirements and determine whether suitable resources can be provided and reserved.

**Step 9 - Event Preparation**: The Event Coordinator monitors outstanding arrangements. Venue Staff and Technical Support Staff update the relevant preparation information as work progresses.

**Step 10 - Event Confirmation**: When the essential arrangements have been completed, the Event Coordinator confirms the event. The Event Organiser can then view the confirmed arrangements.

**Step 11 - Attendee Registration**: Where registration is required, Attendees can register for the confirmed event during the permitted registration period and subject to the applicable capacity.

**Step 12 - Changes Before the Event**: The Event Organiser may subsequently request changes. The Event Coordinator determines whether those changes affect venue, equipment, technical-support, registration, or other arrangements.

**Step 13 - Event Delivery**: Venue Staff prepare the venue and Technical Support Staff prepare the necessary equipment or support. Relevant users should be able to access the latest confirmed information.

**Step 14 - Completion**: Once the event has taken place, it can be marked as completed. Relevant attendance information, operational notes, or issues may then be recorded and the event can be closed.

**6. Notifications**

Users should be kept informed when important events or arrangements relevant to them change. Notifications may be provided within the application or through another suitable communication channel.

Examples of situations that may generate a notification include:

A new event request is submitted.

An Event Coordinator is assigned.

Additional information or amendment is requested.

An event request is approved, rejected, or returned.

A venue booking is requested, approved, rejected, or changed.

Requested equipment is confirmed or found to be unavailable.

An event becomes confirmed.

The Event Organiser requests a significant change.

An event is rescheduled, postponed, or cancelled.

Registration opens or closes.

Registration reaches capacity or a waiting-list status changes.

A registered Attendee withdraws where that affects availability.

An upcoming event still has incomplete arrangements.

A venue or equipment availability change affects an upcoming event.

**7. Design**

The system should be both desktop- and mobile-friendly. External users may access the system from personal computers or mobile devices, while internal ConnectSphere staff may need access while preparing event spaces or equipment.

Information should be presented clearly and should not assume that users understand ConnectSphere's internal processes. The current status of an event, its confirmed arrangements, and any outstanding actions should be easy for the appropriate user to understand.

**8. Other requirements**

**a. Performance**

Common operations such as viewing an event, searching available venues, opening a venue calendar, checking equipment availability, or submitting a registration should complete within a reasonable time.

**b. Security**

The system should only allow authorised users to access protected information. Access should depend on the user's role and relationship to an event. For example, an Event Organiser should not normally be able to view events belonging to unrelated clients, and an Attendee should not be able to view internal planning information.

**c. Usability**

All groups of users should be able to complete their common activities without extensive training or guidance.

**d. Reliability and consistency**

The system should maintain consistent information when related event arrangements change. Users should not be presented with contradictory information regarding event dates, venue bookings, equipment availability, or registration status.

**e. Scalability**

The proposed solution should support ConnectSphere's anticipated growth over the next three years, including increases in events, users, client organisations, venues, equipment, and registrations.

**f. Auditability**

Important actions should be recorded. Where appropriate, ConnectSphere should be able to determine what was changed, who changed it, and when the change was made.

**g. Maintainability**

The organisation expects its processes to evolve over time. The proposed system should therefore be designed so that future functionality and business rules can be added without requiring the entire system to be rebuilt.

**_Notes:_**

The customer will continue to discuss the proposed system with Event Organisers, Event Coordinators, Venue Staff, Technical Support Staff, and other relevant stakeholders. There may be special cases and business rules that have not been described in this initial briefing.

Students are expected to use the scheduled customer Q&A sessions to clarify such matters and develop appropriate epics and user stories. The customer will subsequently identify the functionality considered most important for the first release.

The teaching team will release the exact project deliverables and grading rubrics in Week 4.

257	#### [#80](https://github.com/SinYang13/IS212-2026/discussions/80) [T3] What is the difference between an event being approved and being confirmed?
258	
259	**`important`** · **Ryan-Lee-2000** · 2026-08-25 · 1 upvote
260	
261	> The briefing indicates that an Event Coordinator first approves an event request so that planning can proceed, then later confirms the event once the essential arrangements are completed.
262	>
263	> Could you clarify:
264	>
265	> 1. What does approval commit ConnectSphere to?
266	> 2. Which arrangements are considered essential before confirmation?
267	> 3. Do the required arrangements depend on the particular event?
268	> 4. Can an event be confirmed while non-essential actions remain outstanding?
269	> 5. Should the system prevent confirmation when a required arrangement is incomplete?
270	
271	**Answer** — SinYang13, 2026-08-31
272	
273	> 1) Approval means the request contains sufficient information for planning to proceed. It does not commit ConnectSphere to a confirmed venue, equipment, technical support, registration setup, or final event delivery.
274	> 2) Essential arrangements are those required for that particular event to proceed. These may include venue, equipment, technical support, programme, registration setup, or other event-specific arrangements. There is no single fixed list that applies to every event.
275	> 3) Yes. The required arrangements depend on the event's actual needs. For example, some events may not require equipment, technical support, or attendee registration.
276	> 4) Yes, provided all arrangements considered essential for that event have been completed. Non-essential follow-up actions may remain outstanding if they do not prevent the event from being ready for confirmation.
277	> 5) Yes. If an arrangement has been identified as required/essential for that event and is still incomplete, the event should not be confirmable.

title: Event Lifecycle
type: concept
sources:
  - Customer Brief no. 1.md
  - IS212 2026 Discussions Aug 31.md
  - IS212 2026 Discussions Aug 26.md
tags:
  - event-status
  - state-machine
  - business-rules
  - connectsphere
---

# Event Lifecycle

The set of statuses an event passes through in the [[event-planning-venue-booking-system]], and the rules governing transitions between them. The lifecycle is the backbone that [[event-request-workflow]], [[event-readiness]], and [[change-impact-management]] all attach to.

## Statuses

The brief lists the following as an example set — "Events progress through suitable statuses so that users can understand their current stage, for example draft, submitted, under review, approved, planning, awaiting arrangements, confirmed, completed, cancelled, or rejected" (Source: customer-brief-no-1).

| Status | Meaning | Set by |
|---|---|---|
| Draft | Request saved but not submitted; incomplete information may be completed later | Event Organiser |
| Submitted | Request sent to ConnectSphere, awaiting coordinator assignment | Event Organiser |
| Under review | Assigned Event Coordinator is reviewing; clarifications may be requested | Event Coordinator |
| Approved | Sufficient information exists for planning to proceed | Event Coordinator |
| Planning | Venue, equipment, technical support and programme work in progress | Event Coordinator |
| Awaiting arrangements | One or more essential arrangements remain incomplete | System / Event Coordinator |
| Confirmed | All essential arrangements complete; arrangements visible to the Event Organiser | Event Coordinator |
| Completed | Event has taken place and been closed | Event Coordinator, or system after 7 days |
| Cancelled | Event will not proceed; reservations released | Assigned Event Coordinator only |
| Rejected | Request declined at review; decision record retained | Event Coordinator |

> **Team decision required:** The customer named these statuses "for example" and did not fix the state machine. The exact status set, the transitions permitted between them, and whether *planning* and *awaiting arrangements* are distinct states or one state with a readiness flag are all for the team to propose (Source: customer-brief-no-1; is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #70).

## Approved vs Confirmed

The single most load-bearing distinction in the lifecycle, clarified in full on 2026-08-31 (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #80).

| Dimension | Approved | Confirmed |
|---|---|---|
| What it asserts | The request contains sufficient information for planning to proceed | The essential arrangements for that event are complete |
| Commitment | **None** to venue, equipment, technical support, registration setup, or final delivery | ConnectSphere commits to the arrangements; the Event Organiser can view them |
| Position in flow | Step 5 of the 14-step process | Step 10 of the 14-step process |
| Precondition | Coordinator judges information adequate after review and clarification | All arrangements identified as essential for that event are complete |

Key consequences of #80:

- Approval is an **information-sufficiency gate**, not a resource commitment. Nothing is reserved by approving.
- Confirmation is a **readiness gate**. See [[event-readiness]] for what counts as essential.
- An event **may** be confirmed while non-essential follow-up actions remain outstanding, provided every essential arrangement is complete (#80, answer 4).
- The system **should block confirmation** when an arrangement identified as required for that event is still incomplete (#80, answer 5).

## Completion

- After the event has taken place, the Event Coordinator can mark it as completed.
- If it remains open, the system **may automatically mark it completed 7 days after the event end date** (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #71).
- At completion, attendance information, operational notes, or issues may be recorded and the event closed (Source: customer-brief-no-1, step 14).
- Completed and cancelled events remain available as historical records; there is no retention policy and archival is out of scope (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #20). See [[non-functional-requirements]].

## Cancellation

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| Who may cancel? | **Only the Event Coordinator in charge of that event** |
| At what stage? | **Any stage** |

(Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #68)

This is narrower than the brief, which says "an authorised user can cancel an event" (Source: customer-brief-no-1). The Q&A answer scopes that to the assigned coordinator alone — Event Organisers cannot cancel directly and must route a cancellation through their coordinator. Related venue and equipment reservations must no longer remain committed to a cancelled event (Source: customer-brief-no-1); see [[venue-booking]] and [[equipment-management]].

## Postponement vs Cancellation

There is no separate *postponed* status in the customer's answer. Postponement is resolved into two existing paths (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #69):

| Case | Treatment | Effect on arrangements |
|---|---|---|
| Postponed **with** a new date/time | Treat as a **rescheduling request** | Review affected arrangements — see [[change-impact-management]] |
| Postponed **with no** new date known | Release current bookings, **retain the event record** until a new date is provided | Venue and equipment released; event not cancelled |
| Cancelled | Terminal; only the assigned coordinator may set it | Reservations released, event closed |

The distinguishing property of postponement is that the event record survives — the client relationship and requirements are preserved for a later date, whereas cancellation ends the event.

> **Team decision required:** The customer did not name a status for "postponed, date unknown". The team must decide whether this is a distinct status, a flag on an existing status, or a return to *approved*/*planning* with dates cleared.

## Rejection and Resubmission

Rejected or returned requests must retain an appropriate record of the decision (Source: customer-brief-no-1, step 5).

> **Team decision required:** Whether a rejected event can be resubmitted, or whether rejection is final, was explicitly **not specified**. The customer's full answer was "Please propose an appropriate approach if needed." (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #67). Options for the team: rejection is terminal and a new request must be created; rejection returns the request to draft for amendment and resubmission; or a distinct *returned for amendment* outcome is separated from a terminal *rejected*.

## Re-entrant Transitions

The lifecycle is not strictly forward-only:

- A confirmed event may need to move back to planning when a major change occurs (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #70) — see [[change-impact-management]].
- Rescheduling via the calendar must still follow the relevant event-change process and must not bypass required checks or approvals (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #3).
- There is **no change cut-off period** before the event date, so backward transitions remain possible up to delivery (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #8).

## Cross-Cutting Rules

- Status changes are notification triggers: submission, coordinator assignment, approval/rejection/return, confirmation, reschedule, postponement, cancellation (Source: customer-brief-no-1, s6). See [[notifications]].
- Significant status actions are captured in activity history — what changed, who changed it, when (Source: customer-brief-no-1, s8f).
- Visibility of a status and its underlying detail depends on role and relationship to the event. See [[access-control]] and [[user-roles]].
- The current status, confirmed arrangements, and outstanding actions must be easy for the appropriate user to understand without knowledge of ConnectSphere's internal processes (Source: customer-brief-no-1, s7).

## Open Items

| Item | Status | Reference |
|---|---|---|
| Exact status set and permitted transitions | Team to propose | #70, brief |
| Rejected event resubmission | **Unspecified — team to propose** | #67 |
| Status representation for indefinite postponement | Team to propose | #69 |
| Whether auto-completion at +7 days is mandatory or optional ("may") | Team to interpret | #71 |

See [[open-questions]] for the consolidated list.

# User Roles

The actors recognised by the [[event-planning-venue-booking-system]]. Roles determine both responsibility in [[event-request-workflow]] and visibility under [[access-control]]. [[connectsphere-event-services]] employs approximately 500 staff across the internal roles (Source: customer-brief-no-1).

## Briefed Roles

The customer brief names exactly five roles and states that these "are the roles referred to throughout this customer briefing" (Source: customer-brief-no-1, s3).

| Role | Internal / External | Main Responsibility | Key system actions |
|---|---|---|---|
| Event Organiser | **External** | Client representative who has an event to organise and communicates event requirements to ConnectSphere | Create/save draft and submit event requests, supply requirements, request changes, view confirmed arrangements, view/export attendee information for their own events |
| Event Coordinator | Internal | Assigned to coordinate the overall planning of an event; the main internal point of contact | Review and approve/reject/return requests, request clarification, search venues and raise venue booking requests, record equipment requirements, track readiness, confirm the event, cancel the event, set the registration period, mark completion |
| Venue Staff | Internal | Responsible for venue information, availability, booking decisions, and physical venue preparation | Maintain the venue catalogue and operating hours, approve/reject venue booking requests and suggest alternatives, block venues, record setup/teardown/turnaround, prepare the venue |
| Technical Support Staff | Internal | Responsible for equipment, technical requirements, equipment reservations, and technical support for events | Maintain the equipment catalogue and operational status, check availability, reserve equipment, record defects on return, provide on-site support |
| Attendee | **External** | Participant who registers for and attends an event | Register for confirmed events where enabled, join a waiting list, withdraw, view registration status and open events |

Detail on each role's domain lives in [[venue-booking]], [[equipment-management]], [[technical-support]], and [[attendee-registration]].

## Gap: The Event Operations Manager

> **⚠️ Gap between the brief and the clarifications.** A sixth role — the **Event Operations Manager** — appears only in the Q&A discussions and is **absent from the customer brief's role table, feature list, and 14-step process**. This is not a contradiction: nothing in the brief denies the role's existence, and the brief itself says "there may be special cases and business rules that have not been described in this initial briefing" (Source: customer-brief-no-1). It is a genuine omission that the team must resolve, because a role with no entry in the briefed access-control model now holds the coordinator-assignment authority.

What the discussions establish:

| Fact | Source |
|---|---|
| After an event request is submitted, an **Event Operations Manager assigns an Event Coordinator** to the event | is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #73 |
| Choice of coordinator is **entirely up to the Event Operations Manager**, who follows an SOP maintained **outside the system** — no criteria need to be encoded | is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #93 |
| **Reassignment** of an event to a different coordinator is also performed by the Event Operations Manager; the request and approval process happens outside the system, and the system may assume any reassignment entered by the manager has already been approved | is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #94 |

Consequences:

- The brief's *Coordinator Assignment* feature has no named actor; #73/#94 supply one. Step 3 of the 14-step process ("An Event Coordinator is assigned") is therefore performed by a role not in the brief's role table.
- The Event Operations Manager is **internal** by implication but has no briefed responsibility statement, no dashboard definition, and no stated visibility scope.
- Only assignment and reassignment are attributed to this role. Every other decision remains with the roles in the briefed table — notably, cancellation stays with the assigned Event Coordinator alone (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #68). See [[event-lifecycle]].

> **Team decision required:** Whether to model the Event Operations Manager as a distinct sixth role, as a permission held by a senior Event Coordinator, or as an out-of-system actor whose decisions are simply recorded. The team must also define its visibility scope, since neither the brief nor the Q&A specifies what events or information the role can see.

Note that #93 and #94 were answered on 2026-08-31 and do **not** appear in the earlier snapshot (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-26); #73 was already answered on 2026-08-25 and is present in both.

## Rules Governing Role Assignment

### A person may hold multiple roles

Confirmed without qualification — a Venue Staff member may also be an Attendee at another event (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #56). The system must therefore model **role as a many-to-many relationship with the user**, not as a single field, and must resolve permissions per event rather than per account. See [[access-control]].

### No administrator or system-configuration role

There is no admin role above the five briefed stakeholders. The customer states that no system-configuration feature is specified and that **user administration is not defined as a separate business role**; if a solution requires user-administration permissions, the team may propose an approach alongside the existing access-control requirements (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #52).

> **Team decision required:** Whether to introduce an administrative capability at all. This interacts directly with #49 (no onboarding feature specified) and #64 (no account recovery specified) — if nobody can create or restore accounts, the system has no way to bootstrap its own users. See [[access-control]].

### Staff are not scoped by venue, equipment type, or location

Access depends on role and responsibilities, but Venue Staff and Technical Support Staff are explicitly **not restricted by venue, equipment type, or location** (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #66). Any Venue Staff member may act on any venue; any Technical Support Staff member may act on any equipment. This removes a whole class of territory/ownership modelling from scope.

Related: no separate staff self-declaration of availability is required, and there is no fixed roster update frequency or mandated assignment mechanism for Technical Support Staff (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #88, #89). See [[technical-support]].

### No primary contact per client organisation

Multiple Event Organisers may belong to the same client organisation, but **no primary-contact or client-administrator role has been specified**; the customer invites a proposal if one is needed (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #65). Combined with #81, this means intra-organisation access is a **fixed system rule**, not something a client-side administrator grants. See [[access-control]].

### Delegation is not supported; change of organiser is

| Question | Answer | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Can an Event Organiser delegate their role for a specific event to a colleague? | **No.** Delegation is not supported. | #61 |
| What is supported instead? | **Change of Event Organiser** — the responsible organiser is replaced, not shared | #61 |
| What happens to events when an Event Organiser's account is deactivated? | Use the change-of-Event-Organiser mechanism; events are not orphaned | #59 |

(Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #61, #59)

Implication: responsibility for an event is held by exactly **one** Event Organiser at a time. There is no co-organiser, no temporary stand-in, and no per-event grant of edit rights. Colleagues in the same client organisation get view-only access automatically under #81 — see [[access-control]].

### Event Coordinator assignment mechanics

- A coordinator **can be assigned to two or more events concurrently** (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #92) — no workload cap is defined.
- There is **no acceptance step**. Assignment takes effect immediately and a coordinator cannot reject or decline it in the system; any issue is handled outside the system (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #95).
- Assignment and reassignment are both notification triggers. See [[notifications]].

## Open Items

| Item | Status | Reference |
|---|---|---|
| Whether the Event Operations Manager is modelled as a system role, and its visibility scope | **Gap — team to propose** | #73, #93, #94 |
| Whether any user-administration capability exists, and who holds it | **Unspecified — team to propose** | #52 |
| Whether a primary contact per client organisation is introduced | **Unspecified — team to propose** | #65 |
| Workload or concurrency limits on Event Coordinator assignment | None specified | #92 |
| How Technical Support Staff availability is maintained for assignment | Team to propose | #88, #89 |

See [[open-questions]] for the consolidated list.

# Access Control

Authentication and authorisation rules for the [[event-planning-venue-booking-system]]. The governing principle from the brief: "The system should only allow authorised users to access protected information. Access should depend on the user's **role and relationship to an event**" (Source: customer-brief-no-1, s8b). Roles themselves are defined in [[user-roles]].

Access control is two-dimensional throughout: **role** (what kind of user) combined with **relationship** (which events this specific user is connected to). Neither alone is sufficient.

## Authentication

| Aspect | Position | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Is authentication required? | **Yes** — secure authentication is required | #62, brief s4 |
| Which method? | **Not specified** — email/password, SSO and MFA were all asked about and none was chosen | #62 |
| Account recovery / locked accounts? | **Not specified in the current requirements** | #64 |
| External user onboarding? | **Not in the feature list** | #49, #53 |

> **Team decision required:** The authentication method. The customer's full answer to "email/password, SSO, or MFA?" was "Secure authentication is required, but the authentication method is not specified. Please propose an appropriate approach." (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #62).

> **Team decision required:** Account recovery and locked-account handling. Explicitly out of the stated requirements (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #64) — but a system with authentication and no recovery path is not usable in practice, so the team should decide whether to propose one or consciously defer it.

### Account provisioning gap

Two answers together leave the system with no defined way to create its own users:

- "How do external users (Event Organisers, Attendees) get accounts? Self-registration? Invitation by ConnectSphere?" → "The onboarding process feature is currently not in the list of features as yet." (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #49)
- "Do attendees need an account to register attendance?" → "The system supports Attendees as external users who can register for events and view their registration status. **External user onboarding features are not listed in the brief yet**" (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #53)

Combined with #52 — no admin role and no user-administration business role defined (see [[user-roles]]) — nothing in the specified scope creates accounts for either internal or external users.

> **Team decision required:** How users come to exist. Options: self-registration for external users, invitation issued by an Event Coordinator, pre-seeded internal accounts, or treating provisioning as out of scope with seeded data. #53 confirms Attendees are *users* of the system (they "register for events and view their registration status"), so an Attendee identity of some kind is required even if onboarding is not built.

## Protected Information

Clarified on 2026-08-31 (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #91). Protected information is information that should only be accessible to authorised users **based on their role and relationship to the event**. The customer's enumeration:

| Category | Examples |
|---|---|
| Internal planning information | Coordinator notes, review and clarification exchanges, outstanding actions, readiness state |
| Venue and equipment arrangements | Booking decisions, holds, reservations, availability blocks |
| Attendee information | Registration records and attendee personal data |
| Client-related information | Client organisation records and their event history |
| Other non-public event details | Anything not published to the general audience of an event |

Access follows the user's role and responsibility for the event.

> **Team decision required:** The exact access-control design and **field-level permissions** are explicitly delegated to the solution team (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #91). This is the highest-leverage open item on this page — the customer has given the categories but not the matrix.

Note that #91 was asked on 2026-08-28 and answered on 2026-08-31; it does not appear in the earlier snapshot (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-26).

## Client Organisation Visibility

The brief states only that "an Event Organiser should not normally be able to view events belonging to unrelated clients" (Source: customer-brief-no-1, s8b). The precise rule was left open in the earlier snapshot — #81 is listed as **unanswered** as of 2026-08-25 (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-26) — and answered on 2026-08-31.

**The rule** (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #81):

| Relationship of the Event Organiser to the event | View | Edit / Update |
|---|---|---|
| Responsible for the event | ✅ | ✅ |
| Belongs to the **same client organisation**, not responsible for the event | ✅ | ❌ |
| Belongs to an **unrelated client organisation** | ❌ | ❌ |

Three consequences:

- Visibility inside a client organisation is **automatic and organisation-wide**. It is not granted per event by another Organiser, and it is not administered by a primary contact — no primary-contact role exists (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #65). See [[user-roles]].
- Edit rights are held by **exactly one** Event Organiser per event. Delegation is not supported; transferring responsibility requires a change of Event Organiser (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #61, #59).
- Cross-client isolation is a hard boundary, not a default. The brief's "not normally" is tightened by #81 to "must not access".

This rule scopes [[reporting]] as well: Event Organisers can view or export attendee information **for events they organise**, subject to access restrictions (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #32).

## Attendee Restrictions

- An Attendee **must not be able to view internal planning information** (Source: customer-brief-no-1, s8b) — that is, the internal-planning, venue/equipment arrangement, and client categories from #91.
- Attendees may view events they have registered for **and** events open for registration (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #10). Discoverability of open events is therefore intentional and is not a leak of protected information.
- Attendees see their own registration status; there is no stated visibility of other attendees' registrations. See [[attendee-registration]].

## Internal Staff Scope

Venue Staff and Technical Support Staff have access to the information needed for their responsibilities and are **not restricted by venue, equipment type, or location** (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #66). Internal staff scope is therefore functional, not territorial. See [[user-roles]].

## Role-Based Dashboards

The brief requires that "the system provides each internal or external role with an overview relevant to its responsibilities, such as events requiring attention, upcoming bookings, equipment requests, or attendee registrations" (Source: customer-brief-no-1, s4). Related requirements:

- The event calendar shows information that **depends on the user's role and access rights** (Source: customer-brief-no-1, s4).
- Information should not assume users understand ConnectSphere's internal processes; current status, confirmed arrangements, and outstanding actions must be clear to the appropriate user (Source: customer-brief-no-1, s7).

Indicative dashboard content per role:

| Role | Relevant overview |
|---|---|
| Event Organiser | Own events by status, own drafts, clarification requests awaiting response, confirmed arrangements, registration counts for own events |
| Event Coordinator | Assigned events requiring attention, pending venue/equipment decisions, incomplete arrangements, upcoming events — see [[event-readiness]] |
| Venue Staff | Incoming venue booking requests, upcoming bookings, blocked venues — see [[venue-booking]] |
| Technical Support Staff | Equipment requests to review, upcoming reservations, on-site support assignments — see [[technical-support]] |
| Attendee | Registered events, waiting-list positions, open events, registration status |

> **Team decision required:** Dashboard composition per role. The brief gives examples ("such as"), not a specification, and the customer has consistently returned UI/UX questions to the team ("This is a UI/UX question, please propose and do the appropriate" — Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #6, #27).

Since a person may hold multiple roles (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #56), the dashboard must resolve the **union** of that user's roles, and permission checks must be evaluated per event rather than per account.

## Auditability

Access control is supported by, but distinct from, the audit requirement: important actions are recorded so ConnectSphere can determine what was changed, who changed it, and when (Source: customer-brief-no-1, s8f). The technical mechanism is for the team to propose (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #14). Change history is itself protected — "users with **appropriate access** can review how important event information has changed over time" (Source: customer-brief-no-1, s4). See [[non-functional-requirements]].

## Open Items

| Item | Status | Reference |
|---|---|---|
| Authentication method | **Unspecified — team to propose** | #62 |
| Account recovery and locked-account handling | **Unspecified** | #64 |
| How accounts are created for internal and external users | **Not a listed feature — team to propose** | #49, #53, #52 |
| Field-level permission matrix | **Team to propose** | #91 |
| Whether a user-administration permission exists | **Team to propose** | #52 |
| Dashboard content per role | Team to propose | brief s4 |

See [[open-questions]] for the consolidated list.

# Attendee Registration

How Attendees register for events in the [[event-planning-venue-booking-system]], and how capacity, waiting lists, withdrawal, and attendance are handled. Registration is step 11 of the 14-step process and sits downstream of event confirmation — see [[event-lifecycle]].

## Preconditions

Registration is available only when **both** conditions hold (Source: customer-brief-no-1, s4, s5):

1. The event is **confirmed**.
2. Registration is **enabled** for that event ("Where enabled, Attendees can register for confirmed events").

Not every event requires registration. Registration setup is one of the arrangements that may or may not be essential for a given event — "some events may not require equipment, technical support, or attendee registration" (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #80). See [[event-readiness]].

## Registration Period

| Rule | Detail | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Separate dates | There is a **registration start date and end date, separate from the event date** | #30 |
| Who sets them | The **Event Coordinator** | #30 |
| Enforcement | Attendees should only be able to register when registration is available | brief s4 |
| Extension / re-opening | The registration period **may be extended** — registration can be re-opened after closing, e.g. when additional capacity becomes available | #42 |

(Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #30, #42)

Implications:

- Registration windows are per-event data owned by the Event Coordinator, not derived from the event date.
- Because the period is extensible, closure must be modelled as a **mutable date**, not a terminal state. A closed registration can return to open.
- Registration opening and closing are notification triggers (Source: customer-brief-no-1, s6). See [[notifications]].

> **Team decision required:** Whether a re-opened registration period is a new period or an edit to the existing one, and whether waiting-list members are promoted before the period re-opens to the public. #42 confirms extension is allowed but does not sequence it against the waiting list.

## Capacity

- Registration may be limited according to the capacity defined for the event, and the system "should prevent or appropriately handle registrations beyond the permitted capacity" (Source: customer-brief-no-1, s4).
- Expected attendance and venue capacity are considered throughout planning; a significant attendance change may require the suitability of an existing venue booking to be reviewed (Source: customer-brief-no-1, s4). See [[venue-suitability]] and [[change-impact-management]].
- Registration numbers reaching capacity earlier than expected is named in the brief as a routine change scenario (Source: customer-brief-no-1, s2).
- Multi-session events may have **different attendance limits per session** (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #74).

> **Team decision required:** The relationship between event capacity, venue capacity, and the registration limit. The brief treats them as related but does not state whether the registration cap is set independently by the coordinator or derived from the booked venue.

## Waiting List

| Rule | Detail | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Supported? | Yes — additional Attendees may join a waiting list when an event reaches capacity | brief s4, #44 |
| Promotion order | **FIFO**, with **manual override** permitted | #26 |
| Acceptance window | **3 days** for a waitlisted Attendee to accept when a spot opens, before it passes on | #44 |

(Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #26, #44)

The 3-day window is one of the few **hard numeric business rules** the customer has committed to; it should be treated as a fixed requirement rather than a proposal. FIFO is the default ordering, but the manual override means promotion cannot be a purely automatic queue — an authorised user must be able to promote out of order.

Waiting-list status changes are a notification scenario (Source: customer-brief-no-1, s6). See [[notifications]].

> **Team decision required:** Who may exercise the manual override (#26 does not name a role — the Event Coordinator is the natural candidate given #30), and what happens when the 3-day window expires: automatic pass to the next in queue, return to the back of the queue, or removal.

## Withdrawal

- Attendees can withdraw their registration where permitted, and "the released place may subsequently become available to another Attendee" (Source: customer-brief-no-1, s4).
- A registered Attendee withdrawing, where that affects availability, is a notification scenario (Source: customer-brief-no-1, s6).

Withdrawal is the primary trigger that opens a spot and starts the 3-day waiting-list acceptance window under #44.

> **Team decision required:** Whether withdrawal is permitted up to the event date or has a cut-off. The brief says "where permitted" without defining the permission rule; note that no change cut-off exists for events generally (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #8).

## Attendees Who Do Not Self-Register

For attendees who are not self-registering through the system — for example VIPs — **the attendee list must be provided to the Event Coordinator for processing** (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #33).

The question asked whether an *Event Organiser* could manually add attendees; the answer routes this through the **Event Coordinator** instead. Two consequences:

- Event Organisers do not get a bulk-add or manual-add capability of their own.
- The system needs a coordinator-side path to create registration records for people who never authenticate, which must coexist with the capacity and waiting-list rules above.

> **Team decision required:** The mechanism for coordinator-side entry (manual entry, bulk import, or off-system handover with only headcount recorded), and whether such attendees consume capacity and can be checked in.

## Attendance Recording

Registration and attendance are distinguished — ConnectSphere may record whether registered Attendees ultimately attended (Source: customer-brief-no-1, s4).

**Method:** attendance is **manually checked in at the counter**, either using a **QR code** or **manually by staff** (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #38).

- Both paths are on-site and staff-mediated. Attendee self-reporting and automated check-in were asked about and not adopted.
- Attendance information may be recorded at completion, along with operational notes and issues (Source: customer-brief-no-1, step 14). See [[event-lifecycle]].
- QR code implies each registration needs a scannable identifier issued to the Attendee.

## Attendee Limits and Visibility

| Question | Answer | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Can an Attendee register for multiple events simultaneously? Any limit? | **No limit has been specified.** The customer invites a proposal if the solution requires restrictions | #48 |
| What can an Attendee see? | Events they have registered for **and** events open for registration | #10 |
| Do Attendees need an account? | Attendees are supported as external users who register and view registration status; **onboarding features are not listed** | #53 |

Attendees must not be able to view internal planning information (Source: customer-brief-no-1, s8b). See [[access-control]].

## Registration Information Fields

> **Team decision required:** What information an Attendee must provide when registering. Asked directly — "Name only? Dietary needs? Accessibility requirements?" — and returned in full: "Please propose an appropriate set of information based on the event needs." (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #22).

The phrase "based on the event needs" suggests the field set may vary per event rather than being globally fixed; the brief similarly says Attendees "provide the **required** registration information" (Source: customer-brief-no-1, s4), implying per-event configuration.

## Reporting

Event Organisers and Event Coordinators can view or export attendee information where appropriate and subject to access restrictions; Event Organisers may do so **for events they organise** (Source: customer-brief-no-1, s4; is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #32). See [[reporting]] and [[access-control]].

## Open Items

| Item | Status | Reference |
|---|---|---|
| Registration information fields | **Team to propose** | #22 |
| Limits on events per Attendee | **Unspecified — team to propose if needed** | #48 |
| Who may exercise the waiting-list manual override | Not named | #26 |
| Behaviour when the 3-day acceptance window expires | Team to propose | #44 |
| Mechanism for coordinator-entered (non-self-registering) attendees | Team to propose | #33 |
| Whether registration capacity is derived from venue capacity or set independently | Team to propose | brief s4 |
| Withdrawal cut-off, if any | Team to propose | brief s4, #8 |

See [[open-questions]] for the consolidated list.

# Notifications

How the [[event-planning-venue-booking-system]] keeps users informed when events or arrangements relevant to them change. The brief's stated purpose: "Users should be kept informed when important events or arrangements relevant to them change" (Source: customer-brief-no-1, s6). Notifications directly address several of the brief's named pain points — last-minute changes not reaching affected staff or attendees, Technical Support Staff receiving insufficient notice, and Attendees receiving outdated event information (Source: customer-brief-no-1, s2).

## Notification Scenarios

The brief lists the following as examples of situations that may generate a notification (Source: customer-brief-no-1, s6). Grouped by concept:

| Scenario | Primary recipients | Related page |
|---|---|---|
| A new event request is submitted | Event Operations Manager / Event Coordinators | [[event-request-workflow]] |
| An Event Coordinator is assigned | Assigned coordinator, Event Organiser | [[user-roles]] |
| Additional information or amendment is requested | Event Organiser | [[event-request-workflow]] |
| An event request is approved, rejected, or returned | Event Organiser | [[event-lifecycle]] |
| A venue booking is requested, approved, rejected, or changed | Venue Staff, Event Coordinator | [[venue-booking]] |
| Requested equipment is confirmed or found to be unavailable | Event Coordinator | [[equipment-management]] |
| An event becomes confirmed | Event Organiser, internal staff | [[event-lifecycle]] |
| The Event Organiser requests a significant change | Event Coordinator | [[change-impact-management]] |
| An event is rescheduled, postponed, or cancelled | All affected parties incl. Attendees | [[change-impact-management]] |
| Registration opens or closes | Attendees | [[attendee-registration]] |
| Registration reaches capacity or a waiting-list status changes | Event Coordinator, Attendees | [[attendee-registration]] |
| A registered Attendee withdraws where that affects availability | Event Coordinator, waitlisted Attendees | [[attendee-registration]] |
| An upcoming event still has incomplete arrangements | Event Coordinator | [[event-readiness]] |
| A venue or equipment availability change affects an upcoming event | Event Coordinator | [[venue-booking]], [[equipment-management]] |

The list is illustrative ("Examples of situations that **may** generate a notification"), not exhaustive. Recipients above are inferred from role responsibilities in [[user-roles]] — the brief does not specify a recipient matrix.

> **Team decision required:** The recipient matrix — which roles receive which notification, and whether recipients are derived from relationship to the event or configured. The brief lists triggers only.

## Channels

**Both in-app and email**, configurable **per notification type** (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #37).

The question asked whether configuration was per user or mass-configured; the answer was neither exactly — "We should allow both channels but it should also be configurable for the **type of notifications**." Configuration is therefore keyed on notification type rather than on the individual user.

| Aspect | Position |
|---|---|
| Channels supported | In-app **and** email |
| Configuration axis | Per notification **type** |
| Per-user preference | Not stated in #37; the brief separately lists "communication preferences" as profile data (Source: customer-brief-no-1, s4) |

Email is explicitly a **notification-channel requirement, not an integration requirement**: "No integration with existing external applications or services is required for the current scope. However, the notification requirements may include sending email notifications. This should be treated as a notification-channel requirement rather than a general integration requirement." (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #79).

> **Team decision required:** Whether per-user preferences (from the User Profile Management feature) combine with the per-type channel configuration, and how conflicts resolve. #37 defines type-level configurability; the brief's profile "communication preferences" implies a user-level axis that has not been reconciled with it.

## Delivery Timing: Batch vs Real-Time

This answer evolved across the two snapshots and is the most consequential timing decision on the page.

| Snapshot | State of #55 |
|---|---|
| 2026-08-25 (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-26) | Listed as **unanswered / re-opened by a follow-up**. Previous answer: "We will put it as a batch but the frequency should be configurable". Follow-up from JameszLau asking what "batch" means was outstanding. |
| 2026-08-31 (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31) | Still listed as unanswered, but the customer **did respond** in a follow-up dated 2026-08-31. |

**The 2026-08-31 clarification, verbatim in substance** (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #55):

- Notifications **do not need to be delivered immediately in real time**.
- They **may be grouped and sent at configurable intervals**, and the exact frequency **should be configurable**.
- **If real-time delivery is technically simpler, that is also acceptable.**
- The underlying requirement: **there is no hard requirement for notifications to be received within a specific time limit.**

This is not a contradiction of the earlier "batch" answer — it is a relaxation that explains it. The operative constraint is the absence of a delivery-time SLA, not a mandate to build a queue. A team may implement real-time delivery and still satisfy #55.

> **Team decision required:** Whether to implement batched delivery with a configurable interval, or immediate delivery. #55 explicitly permits either. The only firm requirement is that **no delivery-time guarantee is owed**. If batching is chosen, the interval must be configurable.

Because there is no delivery-time requirement, notification latency should **not** be treated as a performance target. The brief's performance requirement covers "common operations such as viewing an event, searching available venues, opening a venue calendar, checking equipment availability, or submitting a registration" — notification delivery is not among them (Source: customer-brief-no-1, s8a). See [[non-functional-requirements]].

## Reminders

The brief's Reminder System feature: the system "may remind relevant users about upcoming events, incomplete arrangements, registration deadlines, preparation activities, or other time-sensitive matters" (Source: customer-brief-no-1, s4).

### Incomplete arrangements

Confirmed as required: "**Yes**, reminders for incomplete arrangements. The frequency would be **by batch** and should also be **configurable**." (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #47).

This answers a direct question about whether the system should "nag" the coordinator about incomplete arrangements or pending approvals. It aligns with the brief's "An upcoming event still has incomplete arrangements" notification scenario and with the Outstanding Action Tracking feature. See [[event-readiness]].

### Reminder timing

> **Team decision required:** How far in advance and how often reminders fire. Asked with concrete options ("1 week before event, 1 day before?") and returned in full: "**The timing and configurability are for you to propose.**" (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #40).

Note the interaction between #40 and #47/#55: the customer requires that *frequency* be configurable for batched notifications and incomplete-arrangement reminders, but leaves *lead time* and the broader reminder configurability model entirely to the team. These are compatible — #47 fixes that reminders exist and are configurable; #40 leaves the parameter values and the configuration surface open.

## Availability Changes Affecting Upcoming Events

An availability change that affects an upcoming event is a notification scenario (Source: customer-brief-no-1, s6; is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #54).

The customer's answer to what happens when a confirmed venue becomes unavailable (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #54):

1. **Venue Staff are responsible for updating venue availability** when operational circumstances change.
2. An availability change affecting an upcoming event **is a notification scenario**.
3. The **Event Coordinator** then makes the necessary changes to the event.
4. "Please propose an appropriate automation mechanisms if required."

Responsibility is therefore split: Venue Staff record the fact, the system surfaces it, the Event Coordinator resolves it. The system is not stated to auto-cancel or auto-rebook. The same pattern applies to equipment becoming damaged or unavailable — Technical Support Staff maintain equipment status (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #9) and the resulting impact is reviewed by the coordinator. See [[change-impact-management]], [[venue-booking]], and [[equipment-management]].

> **Team decision required:** The automation mechanism linking an availability change to the affected events — how affected upcoming events are detected, and whether anything beyond notification happens automatically (#54).

## Design Constraints

- The system must be desktop- and mobile-friendly; internal staff may need access while preparing venues or equipment (Source: customer-brief-no-1, s7). This is relevant to in-app notification design.
- Offline access is **not** a requirement (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #31).
- Notification content is subject to [[access-control]] — a notification must not disclose protected information to a recipient not entitled to see it (Source: is212-discussions-2026-08-31, #91).
- Notification volume interacts with the role-based dashboard, which surfaces the same "events requiring attention" information in-app (Source: customer-brief-no-1, s4).

## Open Items

| Item | Status | Reference |
|---|---|---|
| Batch interval vs real-time delivery | **Either acceptable — team to choose; no delivery-time requirement** | #55 |
| Reminder lead time and configurability model | **Team to propose** | #40 |
| Recipient matrix per notification type | Not specified | brief s6 |
| Reconciliation of per-type channel config with per-user communication preferences | Not specified | #37, brief s4 |
| Automation mechanism for availability-change impact | **Team to propose if required** | #54 |

See [[open-questions]] for the consolidated list.

5	## Architecture
6	
7	- **`raw/`** — Immutable source documents. Never modify these. This is the source of truth.
